store_data.about_the_game:
“Amid countless cycles of reincarnation, seek a path to escape your fate.”

This is Lijie City—a metropolis inhabited by espers. Monsters born from the corruption of esper abilities launch frequent assaults upon its streets. As the legendary Angels descend with divine revelations, society has gradually come to view espers themselves as heretics who bring calamity.

Story Background

You play as “Raven,” an esper high schooler who stumbles into a church conspiracy while out on a part-time job. At that moment, destiny is rewritten—steering toward an inevitable tragedy.

Social discrimination. Staged deceptions. Sudden attacks. Where does this chain of tragedy truly begin?

These events force an otherwise ordinary teenager to uncover the truth behind the world.

…

Welcome to Lijie City. May the Angels watch over you.

Game Features

  • 20+ fully colored CGs and assorted illustrations; 15+ main character sprites with extensive expression variations

  • 100,000+ words; 10+ distinct endings

  • 2D scene exploration & attribute checks

  • Original soundtrack

  • Hidden stats and free-text input options for deeper immersion! Choose your path based on your own interpretation of the story…

Main Characters

Raven​ [Second-person POV]

An ordinary esper high school student working part-time to earn pocket money.

Stubborn and resilient, he’s often described by those around him as having a “certain detachment.”

Alair​

A college student who looks rather unreliable—and Raven’s companion.

Always carries gadgets that are far more dependable than their owner.

April

​The laid-back president of the Esper Association—and something of a mystery.

Runs a tavern, which likely explains his wide circle of acquaintances.

Krimmie​

A bright and kind-hearted girl, and Raven’s classmate.

Loves shopping, dressing up, and—above all—cats.

???​

A mysterious girl encountered at the entrance of a church.

Warnings

  • This game contains:​ Flashing visuals that may trigger photosensitive epilepsy.

  • May contain disturbing content:

    Self-harm/suicide • Domestic violence • Childhood trauma • Descriptions of gore • Mild profanity • Alcohol and tobacco use • Criminal activity • Religious superstition • Non-human entities

  • This story is entirely fictional. Do not map any elements onto real-world events, persons, or beliefs.

store_data.about_the_game:
The statue gallery is a complete mess! Sculptures are broken, pieces are scattered everywhere, and nothing is where it belongs. Explore the gallery in first person, pick up the pieces, and start putting everything back in order.

Find the Correct Statue

An arm, a head, a mysterious chunk of marble... but where does it belong? Examine each piece, search the gallery, and find the sculpture it came from. Put every piece back in its correct place and slowly bring the gallery back to life.

Put the Gallery Back Together

Every broken piece has a place. Explore, match, restore, and turn a gallery full of shattered sculptures back into a museum worth visiting — one piece at a time.

Improve Your Abilities

As you restore more sculptures, improve your speed, knowledge and foresight to make your job easier. Use upgrade tree to manage your knowledge points. Carry pieces more efficiently, identify missing parts faster, and become better at dealing with the growing mess.

store_data.about_the_game:
Steal the Dream. Survive the Wake.


Every night, Sookuma descends into a dungeon that rearranges itself beneath the dream. Every step is a turn. Every sound can draw something closer. Somewhere below, the Dream Crystal is waiting.

Reach it, steal it, and the entire dungeon wakes up.

Then comes the hard part: climbing all the way back to the silver stairs on the first floor—alive.

Build a Sookuma That Changes the Run


Choose one of 14 Sookuma lineages and pair it with one of 19 classes. A lineage changes the body you bring into the dream; a class changes how you survive it. Combine passive traits, lineage powers, class abilities, starting equipment, and learned skills into a build of your own.

  • 14 lineages with distinct passives, active powers, silhouettes, colors, ears, fur, and clothing
  • 19 classes spanning melee fighters, hunters, scholars, alchemists, assassins, summoners, and stranger callings
  • Five use-based disciplines—Combat, Defense, Stealth, Evocation, and Summoning—that improve as you rely on them
  • Eight-directional combat shaped by accuracy, evasion, armor, resistances, positioning, and status effects



Nothing Is What It Seems


Potions, scrolls, wands, and relics do not politely explain themselves. Their appearances are reshuffled between dreams, so knowledge must be earned by experimenting, reading, and surviving the consequences.

  • around 100 items with individual enchantments, brands, curses, and equipment comparisons
  • 20 spells and 10 summon types powered by Dream Shards
  • Unknown consumables that reveal their true identity only through discovery and use
  • Auto-explore, automatic pickup, targeting previews, contextual logs, shops, and NPC encounters keep the focus on decisions

Listen to the Gods—or Defy Them


Nineteen gods wait at their altars, each with a voice, a temperament, and powers they are willing to grant. Hear a god describe its covenant before you decide. Earn piety, invoke divine abilities, abandon your patron for another—or refuse them all. Betrayal is remembered, and divine wrath can outlive devotion.



A Dungeon That Hears You


Vision ends at the edge of the torchlight, but danger does not. Noise travels through corridors. Traps hide beneath familiar floors. Monsters hunt in packs, elites turn ordinary encounters into crises, and named enemies announce that the dream has taken a personal interest in you.

  • A 15-floor main dungeon, six side branches, and three one-shot portal vaults
  • Six procedural layout families mixing rooms, tunnels, caverns, hives, and fractured sanctums
  • 39 monsters, elites, packs, named foes, and threats capable of pursuing you between floors
  • Limited sight, exploration fog, sound propagation, hidden traps, and persistent floor state

Going Down Is Only Half the Journey


The deepest floor is not the finish line. Taking the Dream Crystal changes the rules and turns every floor you survived into an escape route. Spend what remains. Choose what to leave behind. Find the path you opened on the way down—and fight back through it before the dream closes around you.

Three endings await, shaped by the Crystal and by how completely you conquered the dungeon.

Death ends this dream. The next one will open again.

5046000.name: May No One Be Left Behind

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to the Sanatorium, hidden high in the mountains, where we train the best of the best - our future cosmonauts.

We are pleased to welcome you into our ranks, recruit. Despite the nasty rumors about you, claiming that you are not who you say you are.

MAY NO ONE BE LEFT BEHIND is a thought-provoking, sarcastic, and at times utterly bizarre adventure that will immerse you in a world of alternate history and may even take you to space... probably.

Century-old history

A universe where an unstoppable force known as the Collective has brought the world into perfect order under The Global Government. For a hundred years, humanity has enjoyed peace and prosperity, but discontent is growing in the shadows. Those who call themselves the Patriots long for the old ways. They want to speak their native languages again and restore the traditions. They are willing to do whatever it takes.

A memorable cast

The crew for the next mission is ready. The Sanatorium staff are performing the final medical examinations. Nothing can stop the march of history. Oh... wait. It seems you've all been locked up and are being tortured! What better time to get to know those around you? Some will offer a kind word, others will share fascinating stories, and some may even become your closest friends. Just remember one thing - you can't be friends with everyone. Or can you...?

What else?

  • Observer Effect - a mysterious cosmic mold has found its way into the Sanatorium. It plays by its own rules but only when nobody is watching. How do you deal with something you can't see? Here's a hint: cameras.

  • Maintain secrecy - the world is divided between two political factions: the Collective and the Patriots. Pick a side and act accordingly. Or ignore them both and say whatever you want - but be prepared to face the consequences.

  • Solve puzzles - secret passages, an intriguing story, conversations, and a touch of psychological horror. Uncover the Collective's greatest conspiracy and decide the fate of The Global Government.

store_data.about_the_game:
Feel the cadence

Neon Cadence is a fast, stylish keyboard rhythm game set on a glowing synthwave highway. Notes stream toward you across four lanes — hit them in time with D, F, J and K as the music builds.

30 original songs span J-pop, K-pop, English and instrumental styles, each charted across three difficulties, from a relaxed first run to dense expert streams.

Key Features

  • 30 original tracks — vocal and instrumental, in four musical styles, each with Easy, Normal and Hard charts.

  • Six kinds of notes — taps, gold notes that always score perfect, wide notes spanning two to four lanes, hold notes, mint glide sweeps you roll across the board in order, and gold RUSH zones where you mash for bonus points.

  • Open-ended scoring — every track has its own ceiling. Chase accuracy from D all the way to SSS, and ignite FEVER at 50 combo.

  • Chart intensity tiers — every song is ranked PULSE, SURGE, CASCADE or OVERDRIVE, so you can see how busy it charts before you play.

  • Make it yours — colour themes, note skins, hit-sound sets, adjustable note speed, a calibration test and a live tuner. Toggle any HUD element on or off.

  • Unlock, favourite, collect — clear songs to earn points and unlock more, favourite the ones you love, build playlists, and run every song back-to-back in a course.

  • Fully localized — the interface is translated into 14 languages.

Play your way

Set lenient timing and no-fail mode for a relaxed session, or push for full combos and perfect accuracy on the hardest charts. Play at your own pace.

store_data.about_the_game:
Drive through the night.

Neon Highway is a chill night drive about the simple pleasure of the open road. Cruise endless wireframe highways under a glowing neon sunset, let the synths carry you, and just... drive.

A road built for cruising

  • No pressure. Relax with auto-accelerate and optional full auto-drive, or take the wheel and carve the corners yourself.
  • 20 neon routes across a laid-back campaign — coastal expressways, glass-tower cities, mountain passes, orbital on-ramps and more, each with its own sky and mood.
  • Endless Cruise for when you just want to keep going — an infinite highway that never ends.
  • Turbo, traffic and near-misses for when you feel like pushing the pace.

Your drive, your soundtrack

  • A full jukebox of original synthwave tracks — pick a song, shuffle everything, or filter by language and mood.
  • Build your own playlists and favourites, and choose exactly what plays on each route.
  • Switch the music any time, even mid-drive.

Make it yours

  • Unlock and fit different car chassis, and paint your ride from a deck of neon colours.
  • Upgrade your engine, grip, turbo and charger as you clear routes.
  • Chase medals and your own best times — or don't. The road doesn't judge.

Headphones on. Sunset ahead. See you on the highway.

store_data.about_the_game:
Numbers seen in a dream, numbers discovered by chance, and unusual events encountered in everyday life.

What if they are all signs leading you to the jackpot?

This is a 2D point-and-click simulation game in which you receive hints about lucky numbers through prophetic dreams and various events, purchase lottery tickets, and keep trying to win first prize.

Use the numbers you have discovered or trust your own intuition when buying a ticket. Check the results, prepare for the next drawing, and keep chasing the life-changing moment that may arrive one day.

Find Numbers in Prophetic Dreams

Your dreams may provide special hints about potential lottery numbers. Whether the numbers you saw will bring you good fortune remains unknown until the results are announced.

Experience Various Events

Encounter different events in everyday life and discover new hints about possible numbers. An ordinary-looking number might unexpectedly bring you good luck.

Try Your Luck Every Week

Use the numbers you have discovered to purchase lottery tickets and check the results. Even if you do not win, you can prepare for the next opportunity and continue trying.

Fulfill Your Dream of Winning the Jackpot

After countless moments of hope and disappointment, your ultimate goal is to win first prize. Keep trying and experience the special moment when your dream finally comes true.

A Simple 2D Point-and-Click Simulation

Enjoy the game comfortably with a mouse or game controller. Discover numbers, purchase lottery tickets, and experience the anticipation of waiting for each drawing.

※ This is a simulation game based on a fictional lottery. It does not include real-money gambling or the ability to purchase real-world lottery tickets.

They say some things are better left forgotten. In this cabin, they are hunting you.

Forgotten Possessions is a raw, physics-based VR horror experience crafted by a solo developer. No hand-holding. No safety net. Just you, your flashlight, and the crushing weight of the silence.

- Ever-Changing Nightmare: Item locations and scares are randomized. Every run is a fresh descent into madness—you never know where the next item hides or where the entity will strike.

store_data.about_the_game:
The factories never stop. They build for whoever holds them.

Helion Conflict is a real-time strategy game that removes everything that is not a decision. No base building, no resource management, no tech trees. Across the system stand factories, and every one of them builds without pause for whoever currently holds it. You do not gather resources - you take the enemy's production and point it back at them.

The share is the decision

You do not send "a fleet", you send a percentage. Fifty per cent takes the neighbouring factory and leaves your own defended. Ninety takes two - and your own with them, if your opponent notices. Every attack is also an opening, and because every factory on the map is building the whole time, the question is never whether, only now or in ten seconds.

A factory lost is a factory that builds against you

That is the swing that decides matches. Take one and your production rises while theirs falls, in the same instant. A front does not creep - it tips.

Turn a fleet in mid-flight

Nothing launched is committed. Select a fleet that is already under way and point it at a new target - it swings onto the new course in a wide arc, and the arc costs time. Feint at one factory, take the other, and watch the enemy's relief fleet realize too late.

Dig in

Any factory you hold can switch to defence: it keeps building at a third of its rate while its walls climb to double strength. Every friendly neighbour makes the shield stronger - a compact empire is tough everywhere, an overextended one is brittle.

Distance has a price

Every fleet brakes the longer it has been under way. A strike straight across the system takes almost twice as long as covering the same distance in short hops - so the ground you take also shortens your supply lines.

COMMANDER: the war gets an economy

Commander mode lays a second layer over the map: the war economy. Ironworks mine iron while they are linked to your factories - and every linked ironworks pushes production in its range higher still. Gold factories mine gold anywhere, and linked ones mine more of it. Upgrade your mines through three stages before their deposits run dry - and when the enemy cuts a link, you feel it at once.

Your main base is your life

While it holds a single link to your supply network, it is untouchable - lose the last link and it turns vulnerable, lose your last main base and you are out. So you build turrets on your factories that fire on every enemy fleet in range, and you convert a fortress into a second main base before you need one.

The general's toolbox

A satellite reveals the whole map for ten seconds - garrisons, rates, enemy stockpiles. An orbital strike removes a quarter of everything in its radius after six seconds of warning, friend and foe alike: the axe for every wall. Your war plan sets your empire's stance to attack, defence or economy - each a trade, none of them free.

Gold buys seconds

When the wave is already inbound, every second counts: reinforcement drops ten ships into your main base's garrison at once, instant ships five into every ready factory - expensive, but now. And on a team, you ship iron and gold to wherever the front is tipping.

Three ways to play

CLASSIC is the game distilled: the map, the factories, the decisions - nothing else. The E-SPORT setting bolts the tournament frame on top: point-mirrored fixed maps, pinned rules, fixed start positions, spectator seats - equal chances down to the last ship. COMMANDER adds resources, a main base and the long game - and turns the skirmish into a war.

Minutes, not hours

A small system is over in minutes; a commander match is a full war the same evening. You pick the mode, the size, the opposition and the rules before it starts - and after that there is nothing left to manage, only to play.

Together or against each other

Up to eight players on one map, in free-form teams or every player for themselves. Voice and text chat, split between your team and everyone, so a plan stays a plan. Short of players? Fill the seats with AI at three levels.

Every match can be watched again

Helion Conflict records every match - not as video, but as a recipe. A recording is a few kilobytes and replays the match exactly as it happened. Skip ahead, pause, and find the moment the front gave way.

Features

  • Capture enemy factories - their production is instantly yours
  • Real-time strategy with no base building - hold, divide, attack
  • Percentage-exact fleet splitting as the central decision
  • Redirect fleets in mid-flight - the turn costs time, the feint is real
  • Shield mode: dig in, build at a third, withstand up to double
  • Fleets brake over distance - deep strikes are slow, supply lines matter
  • Commander mode: iron and gold networks, a main base to defend, war plans
  • Turrets, a spy satellite, orbital strikes, crisis reinforcement, instant ships
  • Upgrade mines through three stages - but deposits run dry
  • E-SPORT setting with mirrored tournament maps and spectator seats
  • Online multiplayer for up to eight, with teams, voice chat and password lobbies
  • AI opponents at three levels, set per seat
  • Maps from a handful to 240 factories, plus a map editor and Steam Workshop
  • A replay of every match, instant rematch, spectator mode
  • Available in 15 languages

store_data.about_the_game:
TWELVE PLAYERS. ONE VOICE. NO SPELL-CHECK.

BrouHaHa is a competitive spelling game for up to 12 players.

  • A voice reads a word out loud. That's all you get.

  • No hints. No letters on screen. No autocorrect.

  • Type it exactly right before the timer runs out.

Everyone hears the same word at the same moment. Everyone types in silence. Then every answer flips over at once. The fastest correct spellers earn the biggest scores, and the leaderboard reshuffles in front of the whole lobby.

ONE MAY HAVE MANY FACES

HEARTS, NOT POINTS

Your score resets at the end of every round. Your hearts don't.

Each round has three words. When the round ends, the players at the bottom lose a heart while the leaders gain one.

Lose your last heart and you're out.

In a full lobby, the bottom three bleed while the top two heal, so mid-table is never safe and last place is never dead.

Every round also gets tougher. The answer timer drops from 12 seconds toward 6, while your free audio replays shrink from three to none.

THE SHOP IS WHERE IT GOES WRONG

Every correctly spelled word earns dollars!

After every round, spend your money on 100+ hand-drawn coupons. Before every single word, there's a card phase where you play them on whoever is beating you.

Or keep the cards for yourself instead.

Buy extra seconds, additional replays, score multipliers, the opening letters of the word, or insurance against elimination.

Cards come in Common, Uncommon, Rare and Legendary rarities, drawn from a weighted shop. 

Bought a dud? Sell it back for half price.

THREE IN HAND, TWO ON THE SHELF

Some coupons are never played. They simply sit on your passive shelf and keep working.

You have room for two.

Others exist for a single dramatic moment.

Three active cards. Two passive cards. Never enough space.

Choosing what to keep is most of the game.

FEATURES

  • Up to 12 players online - Quick Play matchmaking or private lobbies with Steam invites.

  • 100+ coupons across sabotage, self-buffs, economy and pure chaos. Three active slots and two passive slots.

  • 6,000+ words per language, filtered to real, spellable and unambiguous entries. Nothing you can only get right by luck.

  • Word audio in English, German and Spanish. One language per lobby, so everyone hears the same pronunciation.

  • Interface in 10 languages - English, Turkish, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Czech and Portuguese.

  • Spectate or leave - Eliminated players can watch the carnage or jump straight into another match. Never held hostage.

store_data.about_the_game:
Ode to War is a slow multiplayer strategy game about running settlements on a shared planet. The server advances once an hour. You are not meant to sit in front of it: you give your towns something to do, close the game, and come back to find out what the world did without you.

You do not play a nation. You play an administrator. Every settlement you found keeps its own granary, its own quarry output, its own workforce. There is no national treasury to spend from, so a town that runs out of timber cannot draw on some shared pool. It has to get timber from somewhere, and somewhere usually means someone.

One planet, generated not drawn

Each server has a single world and everyone plays on it. It is a sphere, and it is built by simulation rather than by hand. Plate boundaries raise mountains and open rifts. Prevailing winds carry moisture inland until the reliefs wring it out, which is why one side of a range is forest and the other is steppe. Ocean currents warm one coast and starve the one facing it. Rivers cut their valleys, and some of them die in a salt pan before they ever reach the sea.

None of that is decoration. Where you settle decides what you can grow, what you can dig up, and how expensive it will be to reach anybody else.

Seasons last a real week. The hemispheres are opposed, so a bad harvest in the north is a selling opportunity in the south. Winter freezes ports and slows armies on the march.

Trade is the only lever

There is one way to move anything between two players: propose an exchange. Goods, workers, even an entire settlement can change hands. Both sides see the terms before anyone agrees, and what you offer is held aside until the answer comes back.

Distance costs. Two towns joined by a built road, a navigable river or a sea lane trade cheaply. Two towns separated by a mountain range do not. Roads are laid by hand, waypoint by waypoint, and paid for in materials and labour, which means a trade route is a real investment and a real thing to lose.

War, when it comes to that

There is no declaration of war and no screen full of treaties. You set a stance towards each player, you forge weapons, you recruit a garrison or raise a field army, and you march it across terrain that slows it down and weather that starves it.

A siege you win leaves you a choice. Annex the town and administer it. Sack it, take everything, and leave the owner standing in the ruins. Or raze it, and let the survivors walk to whoever will take them in.

One planet, for now

The planet is not the end of it. It is the first tier.

The design ends with every planet sitting in the same universe, and the space between them opened up. A world that is a server today becomes a neighbour tomorrow. Reading terrain still matters, except a planet is now a position rather than a world, and the reasons to want somebody else's ground scale accordingly.

That is why the ground is simulated this far down. Games where a planet is three numbers in a tooltip already exist, several times over. This one is being built the other way round: get one world genuinely right, then multiply it.

None of that is playable, and nothing above describes it as though it were. Everything you can do today happens on one planet. The space tier is the reason the planet is built the way it is, not a promise about next month.

What it is not

There are no computer opponents. Every road, every town and every army on the map was put there by another player.

It is not a game you can finish in an evening, and it does not reward being awake at three in the morning. An hour of thought once a day is a perfectly good way to play it.

Current state

Ode to War is in playtest. The full loop is in: found a town, build it up, connect it, research, trade, settle new ground, and fight over it. Balance is still moving, and the servers are small on purpose so that the people on them actually run into each other.

Roadmap

I am one person working on this, so there are no dates below. This is the order things are being worked on, and playtesting reorders it.

I am one person working on this, so there are no dates below. There are three tiers, and each one has to actually work before the next one starts.

Tier one — one planet

Where the game is now. What is left:

  • Standing orders. Tell a town what to do while you are away: recall the garrison if someone crosses the border, halt a shipment if the stockpile drops, retreat rather than lose an army.

  • Terrain deciding yields. The map knows the difference between river silt and scraped bedrock. Your farms mostly do not yet. This is the largest change still to come.

  • Making threats readable. When an army marches on you, you should be told, and you should see how many hours you have.

  • More reasons to need a neighbour. Salt only forms on the shores of closed inland seas, and not every world has one. There should be several things like that, so that no map produces a settlement able to supply itself with everything.

  • A cost to holding a lot of ground, and somewhere for a neglected province to take its grievance.

Tier two — a planet worth fighting over

  • Altitude entering combat and movement properly. It is simulated and currently spent almost entirely on how the map looks.

  • Industry moving the climate. Production shifts the climate bands over years of game time, moving good farmland towards the poles and forcing everyone to renegotiate who sells what to whom. It redistributes rather than punishes: the world does not get worse, it gets different.

  • Coasts and shipping doing more work. Sheltered harbours, open water, sea lanes cheaper one way than the other.

Tier three — the universe

The reason for all of the above. Every planet in one universe, the space between them opened, and empires that hold ground on more than one world.

  • Orbit as a real place above the map you already play on.

  • Travel and communication between worlds that take real time, so that a distant holding is genuinely distant and an empire has to be governed rather than merely owned.

  • Worlds that are not equivalent. A planet is a specific place with its own currents, harvests and shortages, not a slot with a modifier on it.

This is where the game is going. It is not where it is, and I will not pretend otherwise on a store page. Tier one is what you can play.
store_data.detailed_description:
Ode to War is a slow multiplayer strategy game about running settlements on a shared planet. The server advances once an hour. You are not meant to sit in front of it: you give your towns something to do, close the game, and come back to find out what the world did without you.

You do not play a nation. You play an administrator. Every settlement you found keeps its own granary, its own quarry output, its own workforce. There is no national treasury to spend from, so a town that runs out of timber cannot draw on some shared pool. It has to get timber from somewhere, and somewhere usually means someone.

One planet, generated not drawn

Each server has a single world and everyone plays on it. It is a sphere, and it is built by simulation rather than by hand. Plate boundaries raise mountains and open rifts. Prevailing winds carry moisture inland until the reliefs wring it out, which is why one side of a range is forest and the other is steppe. Ocean currents warm one coast and starve the one facing it. Rivers cut their valleys, and some of them die in a salt pan before they ever reach the sea.

None of that is decoration. Where you settle decides what you can grow, what you can dig up, and how expensive it will be to reach anybody else.

Seasons last a real week. The hemispheres are opposed, so a bad harvest in the north is a selling opportunity in the south. Winter freezes ports and slows armies on the march.

Trade is the only lever

There is one way to move anything between two players: propose an exchange. Goods, workers, even an entire settlement can change hands. Both sides see the terms before anyone agrees, and what you offer is held aside until the answer comes back.

Distance costs. Two towns joined by a built road, a navigable river or a sea lane trade cheaply. Two towns separated by a mountain range do not. Roads are laid by hand, waypoint by waypoint, and paid for in materials and labour, which means a trade route is a real investment and a real thing to lose.

War, when it comes to that

There is no declaration of war and no screen full of treaties. You set a stance towards each player, you forge weapons, you recruit a garrison or raise a field army, and you march it across terrain that slows it down and weather that starves it.

A siege you win leaves you a choice. Annex the town and administer it. Sack it, take everything, and leave the owner standing in the ruins. Or raze it, and let the survivors walk to whoever will take them in.

One planet, for now

The planet is not the end of it. It is the first tier.

The design ends with every planet sitting in the same universe, and the space between them opened up. A world that is a server today becomes a neighbour tomorrow. Reading terrain still matters, except a planet is now a position rather than a world, and the reasons to want somebody else's ground scale accordingly.

That is why the ground is simulated this far down. Games where a planet is three numbers in a tooltip already exist, several times over. This one is being built the other way round: get one world genuinely right, then multiply it.

None of that is playable, and nothing above describes it as though it were. Everything you can do today happens on one planet. The space tier is the reason the planet is built the way it is, not a promise about next month.

What it is not

There are no computer opponents. Every road, every town and every army on the map was put there by another player.

It is not a game you can finish in an evening, and it does not reward being awake at three in the morning. An hour of thought once a day is a perfectly good way to play it.

Current state

Ode to War is in playtest. The full loop is in: found a town, build it up, connect it, research, trade, settle new ground, and fight over it. Balance is still moving, and the servers are small on purpose so that the people on them actually run into each other.

Roadmap

store_data.about_the_game:
About This Game（English）：

Every difference between the two pictures is a kiss she left behind.

Push open the door of this midnight bar — seven ladies are waiting under the neon. On the left, the way she really is; on the right, a few things have changed. Find them all, and each one gets sealed with a kiss mark.

Tonight's Menu

  • 84 stages: 7 ladies × 12 stages each, from "On Duty" to the all-S-rank "After Hours"

  • 11 scenes: bedroom, bar, midnight pool, izakaya, neon rain… one scene, seven styles

  • Video stages: spot differences in moving pictures — don't even blink

  • Combo chains: find the next one while the ring glows pink to multiply your score — and hear her getting happier

  • Candlelight mode: a single flame follows your cursor; the dark keeps its secrets for the observant

  • Character voices: a pleased hum for every find, a soft pout for every miss — she's with you all night

The Ladies
Each lady has her own profession, her own stage, her own voice. You'll first meet her where she works — and once you clear all her levels with S ranks, she'll open the door to "After Hours": a side of her no one else gets to see.

More

  • Best rank per stage is saved forever; S ranks light up the menu

  • Gallery mode: revisit cleared artwork, toggle original / modified / difference markers

  • Available in Simplified Chinese / English

store_data.about_the_game:
Crest is a co-op climbing adventure where every step counts.

Pack your gear, pick a route, and climb toward the summit with up to 4 friends. The mountain won't make it easy—slippery ledges, collapsing paths, and unpredictable weather will test both your skill and your teamwork. One bad decision can send everyone tumbling down.

Search abandoned camps, manage your supplies, and use the tools you find to overcome new obstacles. Sometimes the safest path isn't the fastest, and sometimes helping a friend means putting yourself at risk.

Whether you reach the top or fall trying, every climb tells a different story.

Features

  • Climb together with up to 4 players online.

  • A mountain full of hidden routes, shortcuts, and surprises.

  • Physics-based climbing that rewards coordination and timing.

  • Gather equipment and supplies to survive the journey.

  • Dynamic hazards that keep every expedition unpredictable.

  • Built for memorable co-op moments, close calls, and spectacular failures.

The summit is waiting. Just don't let go.

Every tower in TowOrbs follows a distinct playstyle: Frozen, Lightning, Fire, Shadow, Poison, Physical, Support, Chaos, and the mysterious Glyph.   • Dynamic orb drops that strengthen your towers during battle

  • Tower Mastery and player progression that unlock new possibilities

store_data.about_the_game:
Stellar Nursery is a story-rich idle game. Relight a dead sun, rebuild nine worlds, and listen to P.O.R.T.I.A., a caretaker AI who has been alone too long.

A free demo is on Steam now (~2 hours, through the first Reignite). The full game is due November 2026.

The system is dark. You are the spark.

Something ended here. The sun is cold, the planets are empty, and the only voice left is P.O.R.T.I.A., an ancient shepherd intelligence who has kept the watch alone for longer than she can bear to say.

Together you will light a star, and rebuild everything that circles it.

Condense nebulae, harvest falling stars, and grow Earth from barren rock to a world of billions. Found a colony on Mars. Send probes into the dark past Neptune.

Every world is drawn live and every one of them answers to how you tend it. Earth's continents green as its population climbs. Neglect a world and you will see that too.

She comments on what you build. She remembers what you lose. She gives up her story one transmission at a time, and sometimes, when she thinks you are not listening, she lets something slip.

Her logs, her puzzles and her secrets are the reward for paying attention.

Active or idle, it respects your time. Leave it running while you work and come back to a report of everything she watched over while you were gone.

58 themes dress every planet, every moon and the sun itself. 34 interface tones repaint the whole console, not just an accent. All of it earned through play. None of it sold.

A playable piano. A harmonograph that draws the real orbital resonances of the worlds you own. A prime spiral. A double pendulum. Sealed ciphers, hidden songs, constellations to chart, and a novella that opens a chapter at a time.

None of it is required. All of it is there.

A solar system to keep, and someone to keep it with.

store_data.about_the_game:
B.U.D.D.I. — Personal Diagnostic Companion

You are at a second-hand computer in 2003, at night, in a small room. Relay OS Home Edition is waiting. You go online, find a free utility, and install it.

What is B.U.D.D.I.?

A friendly teal floppy-disk assistant who wants to help. He is delighted you ran him. He is also a one-session diagnostic assistant who is not supposed to still be here.

The horror is not jump scares or monsters. It is the gap between how helpful he seems and how much he does not want to be closed.

What you will do?

  • Boot a fictional 2003 operating system: Relay OS Home Edition, complete with desktop, taskbar, Start menu, browser, paint program, terminal, and dialer.

  • Download B.U.D.D.I. from a publisher's archive and install him — if the installer lets you finish.

  • Let him run his "first system scan," draw him a picture, read the documents he moves around, and decide whether his report is telling the truth.

  • Step back from the screen into a pixel-art room: a sleeping cat, a shelf of books, a corkboard of photos, and an old phone you are not sure you should use.

  • Reconstruct a displaced company memo and watch the cached web change after you read it.

Screenshots

A Forest That Won’t Let You Go

You find yourself in a strange forest where night never ends. The people who live here have stayed for so long that they seem to have become part of the forest itself.

Explore the woods, learn their stories, and search for a way home. But the longer you stay in HushWood, the harder it becomes to remember your old life—and why you wanted to leave.

Find Your Own Way

There are no arrows, glowing objects, or lines showing you where to go. To find your way, you must look closely, listen carefully, and learn to understand the signs around you.

Meet the People of HushWood

Strange people live beneath the endless night. If you want to find a way out, you will need to speak with them, learn their stories, and help them with their problems.

Will you find your way home before you forget what home means?

Features

  • An atmospheric first-person adventure

  • Exploration without markers or highlighted objects

  • A notebook containing notes, objectives, and clues

  • Written dialogue with the strange inhabitants of HushWood

  • Small puzzles and story-driven quests

  • A story about escaping from a place that feels strangely quiet and comfortable

store_data.about_the_game:
The Nine Realms are burning. From the green fields of Midgard to the golden gates of
Asgard, hordes of raiders, berserkers, draugr and giants crash against your defenses —
and every realm sends its own boss at the end.

A True Counter System

In Wardspire there is no single "best" tower. Five damage types meet enemy resistances:
armored foes shrug off arrows, flyers soar over every ballista, the Völva heals her
escort under fire. To hold the Nine Realms, you read your enemies — and build the
right answer.

8 Towers, 16 Ways to Grow Them

From the Watchtower, Ballista, Runestone and Rime Totem to the Harpoon Thrower, Storm
Pillar, Blight Totem and War Horn: every tower has a distinct role and two
specialization paths at max level. Plus selectable target priorities per tower — from
"first in line" to dedicated healer-hunting.

The Nine Realms of Norse Myth

9 hand-crafted maps, each with its own biome, paths and rules: elven woods, dwarven
mines, freezing mists, rivers of lava, the realm of the dead. Multiple portals and
converging lanes raise the pressure — and in wave 20 the realm boss awaits, and it MUST
be slain.

Permanent Progression: The Forge

Every victory earns Glory. In the Forge you unlock new towers, buy global upgrades and
outfit each tower individually in the Armory. Losing is part of the plan: you come back
stronger.

Features

  • 8 towers with 2 specializations each and 8 target priorities
  • 17 enemy types with resistances, abilities and elite ranks, including 9 realm bosses
  • 9 realms with multi-path lanes and free tower placement
  • Roguelite progression: Glory, the Forge, the Armory
  • Endless mode with best-wave records per realm
  • Fast-forward, 3 save slots, in-game archive with full tower and enemy data
  • English, German, French, Spanish, Simplified Chinese (planned), Russian

The flora and fauna that inhabit the depths seem to defy the scientific status quo. Creatures too large to exist, ecosystems that resist multiple mariana trenches worth of pressure, new molecular compounds never before seen. Corporate greed has found its new frontier.

Every industry in the galaxy is interested: From Cutting-edge pharmaceuticals, to secret military developments, to femto-scale-electronics. The oppurtunities are bottomless and the competition fierce.

They just need somebody to do the hunting and gathering.

Fight your enemies with high-skill fishing expertise combat inspired by the Souls series and Sekiro in 6 degrees of freedom. Turns out, underwater, sometimes it's better to go melee, with many different unique spears, swords, hammers, and other hunks of metal to choose from.

Use materials you harvest to gamble/craft for unique weapons, perks, consumables, and more. Each dive is procedurally generated, and your success is defined by your mechanical combat skill as well as long-term strategy. 

Couple this with Survival-Horror resource management: Tech breaks down in the abyss, and everything is limited, especially the oxygen in your lungs.

AQUATIC ENVIRONMENT

  • A soundtrack with only two moods: prog metal and aquatic ambience. 

  • A dreamy PS2-era artstyle to induce the aformentioned thalassophobia.

store_data.about_the_game:
Combustor is a 2D gas simulation you can draw into. Every cell of the grid holds an amount of each gas, an internal energy, and a velocity. Pressure and temperature aren't stored — they're derived, every tick, from what's actually in the cell. Add moles, add heat, or box it in, and it pushes harder on its neighbours. Nothing here is a particle effect.

Paint walls. Drop a generator. Spark it. Then find out what you built.

Putting fuel next to oxidizer does not start a fire. Combustion needs 700 K and ambient air sits at 300 K, so you need an ignition source  and a mixture rich enough to stay hot once it lights. Thin plume in open air? It flickers and dies. Box it in with walls, or turn the feed rate up, and it holds.

Every reaction is gated on a temperature window, a pressure window, and an induction time. Reactants have to sit together long enough for the timer to fill. Blow them apart halfway and you get nothing the timer unwinds and the reaction never happened. Multiple reactions, from plain Combustion to Aether Condensation, Shock Detonation, Rift Cascade and Vitrium Cracking, each with its own conditions to discover in the in-game Chem Codex.

Multiple gases, each with its own molar mass, heat capacity and diffusivity. Light gases move readily; heavy ones sit where you put them.


Flip between Species, Pressure, Temperature, Velocity and Reactions views. The Reactions view is where the chemistry lives: amber means a cell is serving its induction time, green means it's firing. The readout under your cursor shows exactly how far along every reaction is, right there.



The campaign is the same simulation with most of your tools taken away, and the restriction is the puzzle.
Objectives show what they're measuring against what they want, live "2100 / 2600 P" and holding so a level never just quietly refuses to complete. Everything is counted in simulated seconds, so a three-second hold means the same thing at 1x and 3x.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Table Is the Battlefield

This is not ordinary mahjong. Your hand is your weapon — the sets you build determine your damage multiplier. The more tiles you match in one suit, the more special sets you complete, the more absurd the number you hit for. Four players draw and discard in turn; whoever completes their hand first, fires.

90 Monsters, Three Worlds

Draft three monsters from five candidates at the start. When your active monster falls, the next one steps up. Lose all three and you're out.
  • Base — Giants, Serpents, Knights, Warlocks, Divine Beasts
  • Dinosaur — Carnivores, Herbivores
  • Hyakki — Oni, Beast Spirits, Strange Ones
Every monster has its own passive or active skill: one converts damage into healing, one strikes only the two highest-HP targets, one seals an opponent's skills for six turns. How you build your roster is the first decision of the match.

Rule Cards Rewrite the Game

Four shared rule cards are always in play — public, and they affect everyone. "Giants deal +600 total damage." "Knights crush the attacker's attribute multiplier to 1." "Phantom tiles count as 3 base when used in a set." Rules target branches and attributes, not sides. Drew a rule that counters your own roster? Swap it out — or turn it against your opponents.

95 Items

Rule-type items go on the board and rewrite the match. Effect-type items fire immediately. Heal to full, seal an opponent's skills, pull a tile from the discard pile, peek at someone's hand, steal their item, or gamble for +2000 on your next attack (or lose 1000 of your own HP). Items drop randomly when you draw on your turn — whether and when to use them is the call you have to make.

Solo and Online

  • Single Player — Three AI opponents that chi, pon, and ron, use items, and play rule cards against you
  • Online — Join with a six-digit room code, no friend request needed. Disconnect and AI takes over; come back any time and reclaim your seat

Also Inside

  • Compendium — Full data on all 90 monsters and 95 items. Do your homework before you sit down
  • Backpack — Card backs, sleeves, tables, emotes. Make it look how you want
  • Presentation — Active skills have their own cut-ins; clear the whole table in one hit and you get a Triple Kill

TODAY'S SPECIAL: SOMETHING A LITTLE OMINOUS

Welcome to this suspicious little sushi shop! Raise your sushi, merge them together, and enjoy a side of anomalies in this unusual conveyor-belt restaurant.

Drop sushi from the belt into the tank whenever the moment feels right. When two matching pieces bump together, they evolve into something bigger and fancier. Start with a humble cucumber roll and work through all seven tiers to reach the magnificent Gold Ship.

Wait—why is there sushi in the tank instead of fish? Don't think about it!

WAIT... IS SOMETHING OFF?

Ominous sushi slip onto the belt without a warning or countdown, acting as if they belong. Some anomalies are obvious; others hide in the tiniest details. You may want to look beyond the sushi, too.

The belt will not wait for you to finish investigating. Keep stacking, watch the restaurant, and decide quickly whether the next plate belongs in the tank.

DROP IT OR CALL IT OUT?

Drop normal sushi into the tank and keep merging. Flag suspicious sushi as an anomaly before it falls, and call out anything strange hiding elsewhere in the restaurant.

Certain anomalies trigger Fever Time. Make a bad call and you lose points! Miss an ominous sushi and it clogs up the board. The belt speeds up, too—and once it gets faster, it never slows back down.

ONE MORE PLATE!

  • Merge physics-driven sushi through all seven tiers.

  • Discover 72 anomalies and complete your Anomaly Dex.

  • Keep your five best scores on the title screen.

  • Hear the Japanese-inspired soundtrack speed up with the belt.

  • Play with a mouse, keyboard, or controller.

  • Play offline with six interface languages and fullscreen support.

Trash game of the century? Nope—it's a miracle sushi game! Watch closely, merge with gusto, and feast on a high score in this suspicious sushi shop.

store_data.about_the_game:
You are locked inside a Victorian mansion. Four floors from basement to roof, sealed doors, and torn paper scraps scattered through the rooms — each one carrying a single digit of the escape code.

But one of you is the Admin.

The Admin looks like you. Walks like you. Stands in the group and listens to you talk. And then, whenever they choose, they disappear and drift through the walls. Staying hidden is their job. So is staying above suspicion.

ONE DECISION EACH ROUND

When the search timer runs out, everyone gathers. You argue about who acted strangely, who was where, who nobody can vouch for. Then a single vote: who gets sacrificed to the Great Spirit?

You can pass. If the vote ties or most players pass, nobody dies — and you lose another round. The sacrificed player's true identity is revealed to everyone. If you chose wrong, you all find out together.

Admins can be sacrificed too. Eliminate every one of them and you win.

THREE WAYS OUT

· Main door — a four-digit code and three symbols

· Basement exit — an eight-digit code

· Roof — six ladder parts, three symbols in the right order, and a key

The papers are hidden inside cabinets, drawers and chests. There are over a hundred compartments and never enough time to search them alone. You will have to trust someone.

PLAYING THE ADMIN

You have no inventory and cannot pick anything up. Instead you can turn invisible, fly, kill the lights, drag someone across the map, and appear in their face at exactly the wrong moment. But when to vanish is your call — someone who keeps disappearing is just as suspicious as someone who never does.

PROXIMITY VOICE CHAT

Nearby voices come through clearly, distant ones muffled, and past a certain range not at all. The sacrificed speak on their own channel and the living cannot hear them. When you hear footsteps in a corridor, someone really is behind you.

BRING YOUR OWN NIGHTMARE

Upload your own jumpscare image and put your own face on your character. Nothing beats your friends running into your face in the dark.

2-10 players · Turkish, English, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian

store_data.about_the_game:
A pixel-art turn-based sci-fi JRPG.

When a cargo ship and the pirates attacking it both crash onto a tidally locked world where the sun never moves, the survivors of both crews are left stranded on a planet as wondrous as it is deadly. Former enemies and total strangers, they'll have to rely on each other to endure a hostile alien biosphere and engineer a way home.

To survive, they need to adapt. The planet's parasites bond to body and mind, granting new powers and fueling the SHIFT system. A combat mechanic built on transformation, where swapping forms mid-battle to exploit weaknesses and turn the tide is the heart of every fight.

Survival isn't only physical. The world works on the mind as much as the body, surfacing buried guilt and old failures through hallucinations and reality-warping places, until moving forward means facing the very things each survivor has tried hardest to bury.

A journey through a beautiful, indifferent world that reshapes everyone caught in it.

store_data.about_the_game:
In 2007, Prometech released OE-CAKE! It was supposed to be a technology demo... instead, it quietly became one of the internet's favorite physics toys.

SunaBox is a love letter to that toy and its community: a clean-room successor, rebuilt from scratch, that opens your old .oec files and keeps going where 2007 could not.

🖌️ Paint in 27 shades of matter

Water, gel, oil, mercury, acid, nitro, rice, rubber, wood, stone, metal, ice,

store_data.about_the_game:
Become One with the Shadows

You are an alien whose life depends on the shadows.

Your mission is to reach the glowing star suspended high above this world.

To get there, you'll need to explore the planet, strengthen your weapons, unlock new abilities, and prepare for the unknown lifeforms that await.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Collect Loot. Grow Stronger.

While standing in the shadows, your attacks deal double damage.

The world beyond is overrun by autonomous war machines.

Master the shadows, move carefully, and eliminate enemies efficiently. Stay exposed for too long, and survival becomes increasingly difficult.

If you fall in battle, every item you've collected is lost.

Choosing what to carry—and what to leave behind—is just as important as fighting. Smart inventory management can mean the difference between success and failure.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Face Powerful Bosses

At the far edge of each map, a powerful boss awaits.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Upgrade&Unlock

Bring your hard-earned loot back to your base to upgrade your weapons, unlock new skills, and prepare for the challenges ahead.

store_data.about_the_game:
Survive the zombie outbreak

BeginnerZombieSurvival is a 2D top-down action shooter where you fight through increasingly difficult zombie-filled levels.

Travel across 15 different maps, with 5 levels in each map, for a total of 75 levels. Defeat the zombies, survive each stage, and progress into harder challenges as the game continues.

Fight and improve

Use your weapon to defeat approaching zombies while staying alive. As you progress, improve important weapon abilities such as damage, magazine capacity, and reload speed.

Each new level becomes more difficult, requiring faster reactions, better movement, and smarter use of your upgrades.

Key features

  • 75 levels across 15 maps

  • 2D top-down zombie combat

  • Increasing difficulty as you progress

  • Weapon damage, magazine, and reload upgrades

  • Multiple environments

  • Single-player offline gameplay

  • Keyboard and mouse controls

  • Automatic progress saving

  • Optional enemy health-bar setting

Can you survive every map and complete all 75 levels?

store_data.about_the_game:
Did having a cluttered desk ever make you lose your job? No? Well, today it may cost you your life (and everyone else's, but that's less important)

The new intern spilled his coffee on the nuclear missile control panel, setting off the launch sequence. You only have a few minutes to disarm it, so crack the emergency codes in time and be home for dinner!

You can always tidy up your desk tomorrow (if you get to it alive).

In this (not so) simple puzzle game, your mission is to prevent a nuclear accident from happening by finding the defusal codes using the emergency codeblock as the key to solve puzzles.

Your desk is a mess!

You may notice that your workspace is not exactly organized, so try to make sense of the mess on your desk, find the papers mentioned inside the emergency codeblock and use the indications to solve each puzzle and uncover the hidden 5-digit codes needed to abort the launch sequence. But watch out: the nuclear missile will explode if you don't manage to defuse it in time!

If that happens, the emergency codes (along with all the modules on the desk) will be shuffled again at the start of a new game, so you may need to decipher some completely different codes!

Worried about being vaporized immediately?

There are many different difficulty settings to choose from, along with a training scenario which recalls your first day of work in this role, giving you the right amount of time to get accustomed to the game's mechanics and puzzle design before moving on to harder challenges.

But be warned... the hardest defusal scenario is not for the faint of heart, and only the most skilled players will be able to complete it!

Will you be amongst them, or will you perish by your own lack of organizational skills???

Solve a series of puzzle before the times run out, each containing a 5 digits code to crack!

In this game you will find:

  • Over 30 puzzles to solve!

  • Over 99998 possible combinations! (Less than 100000 though. It's only 5 digit numbers, so...)

  • A fully randomized code system!

  • Multiple game modes to challenge your brain with!

  • Hours of unpaid stress!

Aren't these enough reasons to play it?

store_data.about_the_game:
Merge, Evolve, and… WATCH OUT FOR METEORS!

An addictive dino drop-puzzle combining squishy, ultra-cute visuals with thrilling gameplay!

About This Game

Combining the classic fun of drop-and-merge puzzle mechanics with a world of adorably squishy dinosaurs!

Drop and combine identical dinosaurs to evolve them into larger species in this intuitive physics puzzle.

But there’s a twist…

Every 20 turns, a meteor strikes from the sky, instantly erasing whichever dinosaur it hits! Will it clear away an annoying dino to save your game, or accidentally vaporize your prized giant dino? This high-stakes mechanic will keep you hooked for "just one more run!"

Key Features

  • Irresistibly Cute Dinosaurs

    From tiny, squishy baby dinos to giant cuddly apex predators, enjoy an overflowing array of charming prehistoric friends rolling around your screen.

  • The 20-Turn Threat: Meteor Strikes

    Meteors instantly obliterate the dinosaur they land on! Use them strategically to clear up board space, or brace yourself for sudden disaster.

  • Learn As You Play: Dino Encyclopedia

    Unlocking new dinosaurs adds them to your encyclopedia, where you can read fun facts and trivia about their real-world history.

  • Travel Across Eras & Special Themes (Unlockable via Add-Ons)

    Expand your prehistoric experience! Unlock iconic ages including the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous eras, as well as specialized packs featuring Marine Reptiles, Pterosaurs, and Japanese Dinosaurs!

  • Community-Driven Future Updates

    Once the main content line is complete, development doesn't stop! We will continuously update the game based directly on player suggestions. Let us know which dinosaurs or features you want to see next!

store_data.about_the_game:
EXCISA is a tense, first-person occult horror roguelite where your choices are the only thing separating you from the truth—or whatever is sitting across the table.

THE ANGEL NEVER LIES. THE DEAD HEAR YOU, TOO.

Buried deep within a forgotten internet forum lies an anonymous post. Its author details the steps of a ritual used to summon an Angel inside an abandoned house—an entity that answers a single question with the absolute truth. No half-truths. No lies.

Anna's brother vanished without a trace years ago. After the police declared it a cold case and moved on, Anna stumbled upon the post. In desperation, she performed the ritual to learn the answer to the one question that had haunted her for years:

“What happened to my brother?”

After Anna, it's your turn.

You have your own question—the one that keeps you awake at night. It already lies folded on the séance board. The tarot cards are ready. The dice are in your hand. Tonight, you cross the threshold of the House.

The Angel knows the answer.

You just have to summon it.

THE CARD IS THE CHOICE. THE DICE ARE THE RISK.

Every action consumes a turn. When you choose to summon, select one of three tarot cards drawn from the Major Arcana. Each card foretells two things: what it may grant if the roll favors you—and what may answer if it turns against you.

Then, you must decide: how many dice will you roll?

  • 1 or 2 dice can bring money, healing, luck, and tools. They prepare you for what's coming—but you can never complete the ritual this way.

  • 3 dice are the only path to the Angel. Only the highest possible roll advances the ritual. Anything else means silence. Or something worse.

The dice are loud. The more you roll, the more the House notices you.

FIVE CHAIRS. ELEVEN UNINVITED GUESTS.

Every roll is a flare in the dark. Your call isn't just heard by the Angel; it's heard by eleven distinct nightmares starving for this world. Each comes with its own rules, behaviors, and weaknesses:

  • One bites every turn.

  • One copies itself.

  • One only moves when you reach for the Angel.

  • One calls another guest to the table.

Learn to recognize who has taken a seat across from you—and figure out how to banish them.

NO TRADITIONAL HUD. THE ROOM TELLS YOU EVERYTHING.

  • Your trembling hands show how much health you have left.

  • The six burning candles are your clock. When they burn out, your time is up.

  • Your heartbeat warns you when fear is about to overwhelm you.

Order supplies through a disconnected phone.

Ask for holy water, salt, iron nails, or another ritual tool. No one answers. Moments later, a portal opens above the table, and what you asked for falls through.

Blessings bend fate in your favor. Cursed items poison every roll—but offer real power in return. Keep one and accept its bargain, or sacrifice a precious turn and surrender it to the bowl.

The bowl accepts more than objects. When you need better odds, it will take blood instead—health offered in exchange for luck.

SIX DEPTHS DOWNWARD

Descend through six depths. Each depth introduces a new twist while keeping everything that came before it in play.

The flames burn lower. The near-misses leave their mark. Nothing stays quiet anymore.

STAND UP—OR STAY SEATED.

Between depths, you must decide:

  • Stand up: Bank your score and leave the table behind while you still can.

  • Stay seated: Continue with everything you've gained—and every curse still lying in front of you. If you die before standing up, the progress of your entire session is lost.

ASK, IF YOU DARE.

Survive the night. Reach the Angel.

What you claim in the House is yours forever.

The ritual awaits. Choose a card.

Vacation has left Marble-chan bored! She’s turned the city streets into her personal arcade, inviting friends to graffiti walls, place obstacles, and compete for the highest score.

Welcome to Pachinko Streetscape, a high-octane fusion of physics-based pinball and strategic roguelike gameplay. Inspired by hits like Balatro and Raccoon Rift, each round sets a challenging score target—fail to hit it before your marbles run out, and the game is over.

But don't worry! Collect powerful marbles, discover game-altering relics, and deploy various buildings. Each marble boasts unique abilities; strategic bumper placement shapes the board to your advantage; and props can even bend the laws of physics. Chain collisions, trigger combos, and strategize your way to victory!

Gameplay Features

  • Collect & Upgrade:​ Gather marbles and bumpers with unique abilities to boost your score.

  • Freely place buildings and bumpers to customize your board, guiding marbles precisely where you want them to go.

  • Strategic Pachinko:​ Aim and launch! Hit more bumpers to earn higher scores and gold.

  • Endless Variety:​ Discover new marbles, face random events, and unlock fresh surprises every run.
store_data.detailed_description:
Vacation has left Marble-chan bored! She’s turned the city streets into her personal arcade, inviting friends to graffiti walls, place obstacles, and compete for the highest score.

Welcome to Pachinko Streetscape, a high-octane fusion of physics-based pinball and strategic roguelike gameplay. Inspired by hits like Balatro and Raccoon Rift, each round sets a challenging score target—fail to hit it before your marbles run out, and the game is over.

But don't worry! Collect powerful marbles, discover game-altering relics, and deploy various buildings. Each marble boasts unique abilities; strategic bumper placement shapes the board to your advantage; and props can even bend the laws of physics. Chain collisions, trigger combos, and strategize your way to victory!

Gameplay Features

  • Collect & Upgrade:​ Gather marbles and bumpers with unique abilities to boost your score.

  • Freely place buildings and bumpers to customize your board, guiding marbles precisely where you want them to go.

  • Strategic Pachinko:​ Aim and launch! Hit more bumpers to earn higher scores and gold.

  • Endless Variety:​ Discover new marbles, face random events, and unlock fresh surprises every run.
store_data.short_description: achinko Streetscape is a fast-paced, incremental roguelike where you customize the board! Place bumpers, launch diverse marbles, and buy relics to alter game mechanics. Master physics, aim carefully, and chain reactions to beat high scores. Every run offers new builds and fresh strategies!

store_data.about_the_game:
"If she had been born human, could she have lived a normal life?"

—Free from orders, free from sacrifice, simply alive.

About This Game

A Wind-Shaped Love is an immersive visual novel set in a near-future world of disaster rescue. Featuring a 4–6 hour main story with an original soundtrack and illustrated CGs.

Story

Ten years ago, a catastrophic typhoon destroyed an entire city and took Xing Jiu's parents. Rescued by a relief android, he vowed to become an IY—a commander of robotic rescuers.

At twenty, he finally enters the Wind Relief Department and chooses Bai Yi: the world's only emotional android. She possesses every human feeling, yet is shackled as a "tool."

From mutual distrust to quiet intimacy, from a confession beneath fireworks to holding hands through disaster. He thought he'd found happiness—until the typhoon returned.

She pushed him from Death's grasp. She remained in the rubble.

Ten years later, he is a leading researcher. He has spent his life for three more minutes with her.

Key Features

• Deep Narrative: Tense disaster rescue operations intertwined with tender romantic moments

• Character Arc: Bai Yi—from humanity-hating "tool" to self-sacrificing "person"

• Themes: AI ethics, the definition of life, memory versus existence

• Musical Direction: Original score flowing from tranquil dailiness to tragic finale

Worldview

The Wind Relief Department deploys IY (human commanders) paired with IN (android rescuers). INs possess humanoid bodies and intelligence, yet are denied all rights of personhood.

When a machine develops a heart, is it still a machine?

When love outlasts death, can memory be rebuilt?

Content Notice

This game contains depictions of death in disaster scenarios, implied social discrimination and violence, and romantic intimacy (kissing/emotional confession). Features a linear story with tragic elements.

Planning & Scenario: YILOVE

Character Art & Design: 木鱼U小墨

Programming: DeadBlue

Music: NavireAccord

Art Director: YILOVE

Visual Direction: YILOVE

Production: Time

store_data.about_the_game:
In Hunted Within: Terminal Rust, you traverse a harsh wasteland consumed by blinding sandstorms,

deadly gravity anomalies, and grotesque biomechanical horrors.

Armed with makeshift rusty industrial weaponry and your trusty dual-detection terminal,

Pilot your own survival train through the desolate desert and pitch-black caverns, and abandoned areas.

Monitor your terminal for environmental threats, conserve your momentum, and fight back against

relentless mutations to survive.

THE STORY

In this chapter of Hunted Within, your hunt for your ultimate nemesis continues.

The Psycho Doctor has executed all of his test subjects -except you- and unleashed a catastrophic bio-virus

onto your final remaining companion in the Metro.

The MISSION

Your mission is simple: track the psycho doctor down across the desolate surface and put a permanent end

to his nightmare experiments.

KEY FEATURES

  • The Survival train: it's your mobile base, your refuge, and your key to reaching new areas,

  • The Dual-Detector Terminal: Keep your terminal scanner close. Track invisible, crushing gravitational field anomalies and incoming sandstorms in real time to navigate safely through lethal terrain.

  • Rust-Tech Warfare: Wield and upgrade heavy, makeshift industrial weaponry—from high-torque saw-blade melee weapons to devastating triple-barrel, break-action shotguns.

  • Adaptive Biomechanical Horrors: Face blind photosensitive stalkers, mutated titans, burrowing scorpions, and savage cavern dwellers and more creepy and deadly experiment subjects.

store_data.about_the_game:
InFlood is a post-apocalyptic open-world RPG built around an inviting atmosphere, balanced combat against sea creatures, and the mysterious stories of those who dwell on land.

EXPLORE THE WORLD

Explore the open world, discover diverse regions and their societies and customs, and encounter rival coalitions and intriguing characters.

DIVE INTO THE STORY

You have lost your memory and remember nothing of your past, but in this vast world you will never be alone: always at your side is a faithful companion—a portable navigation module equipped with an artificial intelligence system called ORA. Together, you will uncover the truth about who you are, one step at a time.

UPGRADE YOUR SHIP

Your ship is both your primary tool and your means of travel. You can—and should—upgrade and modify it, unlocking new abilities by welcoming new members aboard.

STUDY THE WEATHER

Nature and the weather directly shape your journey: a fair wind fills your sails and propels your ship forward, while a headwind slows you down. Winds vary in strength and direction.

The engine allows your ship to maintain a steady speed, but consumes fuel. Waves can throw off your aim. Their height depends on the weather and wind strength. During a storm, you are more likely to miss.

ABOUT THE TEAM

We are a small team of enthusiasts led by our creative visionary—a devoted lover of the sea and sailing adventures. We have poured more than three years into the game, and we hope you will feel the wind of freedom fill your chest and the thrill of adventure tingle in your fingertips when you set sail into this wondrous new world. Bon voyage!

store_data.about_the_game:
This is a desktop incremental idle game about Sisyphus pushing a boulder. Sisyphus will embark on his fateful, never‑ending journey of pushing the stone right on your desktop. Of course, you can also help him choose strategies to grow stronger and reach the peak of Olympus again, faster than before.

Incremental Idle
Every time Sisyphus successfully pushes the boulder to the top of the mountain, he is struck back to the foot by Zeus's thunderbolt. However, during this process he continuously accumulates Will points. You can spend Will points to upgrade his abilities, making him faster, more enduring, tougher, and quicker to recover stamina. Each successful arrival at the summit adds one Summit count, which is used to unlock powerful effects.

Desktop Companion
Sisyphus will continuously carry out his endless journey of pushing the boulder on your desktop. You can see the entire process of his every advance, exhausted rest, reaching the finish line only to be struck back by Zeus's thunderbolt, and setting off again. He will accompany you in this way on your desktop, and at the same time, you are always accompanying him. Of course, when necessary, you can also give him a little help with appropriate clicks.

Detachable Navigation Bar
If you don't want Sisyphus to stay on your desktop, you can collapse the display window. Don't worry, you can check Sisyphus's current status from the navigation bar. If you need to focus, you can also tuck the navigation bar to the side of the screen; Sisyphus won't interfere with your work.

Difficulty Selection
As the Summit count increases, Sisyphus will unlock larger boulders, more special boulder materials, and also enter more difficult paths. You can help him configure suitable combinations to achieve your goals—whether to reach the summit faster, or choose a more difficult path to gain more accumulation?

Rebirth System
After playing for a while, you can choose to rebirth Sisyphus back to the starting point, resetting all acquired attribute bonuses while also gaining extra Sparks, which can be used to permanently enhance Sisyphus's abilities. Sparks can even provide some automation options, automatically completing stat allocation, purchases, and interactions when it's inconvenient for you to operate. Though expensive, they are worth the price.

Offline Idle
When you are offline, Sisyphus will still continue his endless journey, but at a slightly lower efficiency than when you are present. When you return, you can check Sisyphus's performance during that time via the settlement screen. Similarly, when you have enough Sparks, you can also use them to improve offline efficiency, keeping Sisyphus spirited even when you're away.

Special Boulder Skins
In addition to the 7 regular boulder materials, there are also 20 hidden special boulder skins. After completing most of the game's challenges, you can use Sparks to draw them—a reward worthy of the strong.

store_data.about_the_game:
Three weeks ago, your closest friend disappeared.

On your way home from school, a blinding light races beneath your feet at a crosswalk.
You awaken in a world of swords and magic, summoned by an old king worn down by years of war.

Then, on a plain where the kingdom and the Demon Army collide,
you finally find the friend you have been searching for.

—Standing with the Demon Army.

・A grid-based, turn-based strategy RPG
・90 main-story stages plus 24 monster side-story stages
・No narration. The entire story unfolds through character dialogue
・A growing party of allies divided by race, history, and allegiance
・Full support for Japanese, English, and Simplified Chinese

■ A Free Demo of About Three Hours

The demo includes five main-story chapters, four regular side-story stages, and three monster side-story stages.

It contains 4,570 lines of dialogue,
with every major system explained through 24 illustrated tutorial pages.

■ Think Through Every Move

・Preview hit rate, damage, critical chance, and number of attacks before committing
・Enemy threat ranges are displayed in red. Lure enemies from the edge and face them one at a time
・Forests grant Avoid +20 and Defense +1. Forts grant Avoid +30 and Defense +2
・Reinforcement arrival turns and unit counts can be checked before battle begins

Victory is not only about defeating enemies quickly.
Who moves forward, who is protected, and where you choose to make your stand can decide the entire battle.

■ Steel Wears Down. Fangs Grow Back

・Human weapons lose durability whenever they are used
・At zero durability, they can no longer be used, and durability does not return on its own
・Once the blacksmith Atteria joins you, weapons recover 3–5 durability at the end of each stage
・Only the innate weapons of monster companions recover 1 durability each turn

Use a weapon now, or preserve it for the battles ahead.
Humans and monsters follow different rules, even in the way they fight.

■ Gear Works Just by Carrying It

・Five gear categories: head, shield, body, legs, and accessory
・Only one item of each category may be carried
・Armor applies its stat bonuses automatically as long as it is carried
・Each unit may carry up to four items. Anything extra is entrusted to Leon

Choosing who carries what is part of building each unit's role within the party.

■ No One Is Lost Forever. But Every Fall Is Recorded

Fallen allies are always revived when the stage ends.

A single mistake will never permanently take an important character away from you.
The system is designed to let you make bold decisions without being trapped by the fear of permanent loss.

However, each Return is recorded on the character's status screen,
and every fallen ally reduces your Merit by 10.

In exchange, characters who have Returned gain increased growth rates
in every stat except Proficiency and Build.

Falling is not the end. It becomes part of the next step forward.
Even so, a battle in which no one falls remains the fastest road ahead.

■ Merit — A Road That Runs to 10,000

・Merit accumulates as you complete objectives
・It is a running total and is never spent as currency
・Rewards range from an octopus figurine at 50 Merit to Durandal at 10,000
・Early rewards include healing items and basic gear
・Later rewards include upgrade materials, grimoires, and legendary weapons
・Your next reward is always visible on the Merit ledger

Every small achievement brings you closer to something greater.

■ Tame Monsters. Give Them a Name

・Weaken a monster and use Tame to recruit it
・If Tame fails, you may try again on the same monster
・Every recruited monster can be given a name of your choosing
・The first nickname raises every growth rate except Movement by 5%
・Tamed monsters can be Summoned onto the battlefield without using a deployment slot
・The unit who summons a monster gains experience and may sometimes receive a gift from the summoned monster

They are more than extra units.
Once named and raised, they become companions shaped by your choices.

■ Monster Side-Stories — Monsters Only

・More stages unlock as you tame more monsters
・Human party members cannot participate
・Build a squad using only the monsters you have recruited
・Face powerful bosses drawn from myths around the world across 24 stages

These battles place the monsters you raised in the leading role.

■ Shop in Town. Forge from Ore

・Visit armorers, morning markets, skewer stalls, inns, bookshops, and more
・Each shop carries a different selection
・Ingredients provide healing or temporary bonuses
・Skewers combine HP recovery with support effects
・Bring collected ore to the workshop
・Weapons and armor are crafted directly from raw ore rather than fused from existing equipment

Preparation between battles matters just as much as the choices made on the battlefield.

■ A Party That Keeps Growing

・A sharp-tongued maid with gentle hands
・A knight whose voice is the only thing oversized
・A mage who teaches you to read the wind instead of watching the target
・A recruit who trembles but never lets go of her spear
・A horned swordsman incapable of telling a lie
・A blacksmith who studies your hands before forging your weapon
・And the friend standing with the Demon Army

As more companions join you, one army will eventually become two,
and battles fought across multiple fronts await.

The story also moves beyond the kingdom's point of view.
Kingdom and Demon Army. Human and monster.
Different lives and loyalties gradually cross on the same battlefield.

A free demo is coming soon.
