store_data.about_the_game:
No dialogue options. Your words are the choice.

Beneath a land governed by starlight lies Asteria, the Labyrinth of Oaths.

An oath once sworn to save someone still endures long after the expedition ended, forcing people into roles within a promise that refuses to die.

Choose one of three companions and approach the sealed Fourth Door. You will not advance by clicking through a list of dialogue options.

“Swing a sword. Cast a spell. Use an ability all your own.”

“Pet a cat. Cook a meal. Throw a pickle.”

Your own words become investigation, negotiation, combat, and—eventually—an intervention in the oath itself.

The world will not rewrite itself to please you

AI takes on the roles of GM and characters. The world’s facts, the nature of its enemies, the terms of its oaths, and the consequences of your actions remain governed by fixed rules.

Persuasion cannot make everything possible. A key that never existed will not appear. Evidence you failed to preserve may be lost. Every person you meet has motives they will not abandon just because you asked nicely.

Freedom of action means responsibility for what follows.

Choose one companion. Enter as two.

Each companion carries different knowledge, fears, and secrets. Your choice changes which evidence you can uncover, which words can reach another person, and which answers remain possible when the labyrinth turns hostile.

You cannot bring everyone. A truth hidden on this expedition may reveal itself differently on the next.

A demanding labyrinth expedition

Asteria is not kind to the inattentive. Defeating an enemy is not always enough, and naming the truth is not the same as proving it. You will need to observe, form hypotheses, question your companion’s words, and sometimes create a path without fighting.

Many expeditions will end in tragedy. Even so, careful observation and inventive thinking can open a way forward.

No single golden answer.

The ending is not decided by one final prompt. What you learned, whom you trusted, what you prepared, and which responsibilities you accepted all shape what becomes of the oath.

No ending saves everything.

The path you took becomes a story that belongs only to you and your companion.

Video and Livestreaming Policy

You are welcome to upload videos and host livestreams featuring RLG: Origins. No prior notice or permission is required.

Both individuals and organizations may use the official monetization features provided by video and streaming platforms.

Where practical, please include the game title, RLG: Origins, and a link to its Steam store page. If your content includes major story spoilers, we also appreciate a spoiler warning for your audience.

Please do not:

  • Redistribute game files or extracted assets

  • Present your content as officially produced, sponsored, or endorsed by the developer

  • Use the game in content that violates applicable laws or the rights of others

store_data.about_the_game:
Daniel Hernandez Florez has fallen into a depressive episode following the disappearance of his boyfriend, Elliot. Nightmares of a corrupted Elliot who can't remember him haunt Daniel. Celia, gifted witch and Daniel's older sister, returns home to aid in the search. When she finally coaxes him outside, Daniel finds Elliot lost and suffering from amnesia.

With little options, Elliot goes home with the sibling duo, where each day they craft spells and take Elliot places to aid in recovering his memory.

As Daniel helps Elliot, his own memories resurface, hidden in the neglected spaces and forgotten objects around his house. Each day brings them closer to uncovering the truth, but something has made its way inside Elliot… and it's only a matter of time before it claws back out.

✧ Rich with history and witchy insight, there's much to uncover in the Hernandez Florez house.

✧ With 100+ unique ingredients and tools planned, there's more than one way to craft successful spells. 

✧ Navigate key branching conversation sections to guide the narrative and gain Elliot’s favor.

✧ With five endings, experience a spectrum of bittersweet growth and acceptance... or be condemned to abandon all hope.

Accessibility

The following features have already been implemented: Alt Text, Audio/Visual Feedback, Closed Captions, Colorblind/High Contrast Modes, Gamepad Support, Motion/Photosensitivity Controls, Readable Fonts, and more!

Extras

These extra features are planned for the full game release.

  • Achievements

  • Photo & Music Gallery

  • Companion Art/Guide Book (Kickstarter Stretch Goal)

Report System

This game includes an integrated error report system for bugs, typos, and any other issues the player may encounter. 

Disclaimer

The supernatural phenomena depicted are based in real spiritual concepts and practices. Please do not attempt to imitate these practices without expertise.

store_data.about_the_game:
Dive deeper. Come back richer.

Long Dives is a layered incremental game set on the ocean floor. Start with a single generator in the sunlit Shallows. Build power, minerals, and biomass. Then Dive resetting your current outpost for permanent pearl upgrades and push deeper into the dark ocean.

Ten depths wait below: the Dark, the Cinders, the Fissure, the Hadal Zone, the Rift. Beyond the Rift, four more that only Ascension reveals, down to the Nadir itself.

Automate the deep

  • Bring the Procurement Daemon online and let it buy, build, and balance for you

  • Auto-sell surplus on the resource exchange with per-resource rules

  • Research four tech trees, from drill efficiency to time dilation

  • Return after hours away and the outpost keeps producing for up to 24 hours offline

More than numbers going up

  • Send your sub on expeditions and mount rescues for stranded haulers

  • Deliver contracts, race urgent orders, and work long-haul Charters

  • Take on Challenge dives with hard rules: Cold Dark, Silent Running, Iron Sub

  • Recover 27 treasures and weather every event the deep can throw at you

Three layers of prestige

Dive to reset the outpost. Ascend through the Rift to reset your Dives. Strike Covenants with the deep to bend the rules themselves. Each layer opens new depths, new buildings, and new pieces of the story hiding amongst the static — the Archive, the Signal, and whoever is reading.

Hunt For Achievements

  • 50 achievements, three of them secret

A Special Father & Child Collaborative Project

Every creative idea, including core gameplay, mech designs and skill mechanics, was fully conceived by my child. I took charge of programming and development.This is a wonderful, heartwarming creation journey for us. We cherish this mech universe we built side by side. To turn wild imagination into a playable game is absolutely awesome!

What You Get

Full access to 15 uniquely designed mechs with exclusive abilities. Enjoy online matches and private battles with your Steam friends.

Game Rules

The battlefield has 5 zones.

3 zones hold energy cores with 3 energy sources each. The other 2 are bonus zones.

Defend your energy cores! If all 3 energy sources of any zone are wiped out for one player, the game ends.

Victory Conditions:

• If only one side loses all energy sources in a zone → the other player wins.

• If both sides lose full energy sources in separate zones → whoever has more remaining energy sources wins.

A match consists of multiple rounds. Each round has 5 turns where players take actions alternately. Deploy your mechs wisely to gain combat advantages across all zones.

After every round, combat power of each zone is calculated. The stronger side claims victory for that zone, disabling enemy energy sources or unlocking rewards: teleportation or unit enhancement.

Step into our mech world and enjoy pure tactical combat!

store_data.about_the_game:
OVERVIEW

KISI: The Deja Vu (기시: 더 데자뷰)

KISI: The Deja Vu is a 3D spot-the-difference horror adventure game based on the uncanny feeling of familiarity — known as "déjà vu."

Players become Dr. Hoffman, a neuroscientist, who must find an exit within a perfectly symmetrical, mirror-image space.

STORY

"I've never been here before... so why does everything feel so familiar?"

As Dr. Hoffman, you find yourself trapped inside a strangely familiar space.

Two perfectly mirrored rooms — somewhere between them lies the way out.
Psychological tension builds as your own memory becomes your greatest enemy.

GAMEPLAY

The horror evolution of "spot the difference"

Beyond simple puzzles — the purest form of the spot-the-difference genre, recreated in full 3D space.

Move between two rooms that look identical and find what has subtly changed.

Atmospheric direction designed to make you doubt your own memory.

Face the uncanny nature of a space that seems perfectly duplicated.

store_data.about_the_game:
Game Keywords: Single-player / Cartoon Ink-Wash Fusion Style / Roguelike / Martial Arts / Card Game

Rooted in traditional martial arts concepts and core card game logic, this game features a unique offensive and defensive system. You will play as a martial artist roaming the martial arts world, gaining experience in randomly generated levels, using cards to attack, block, counter, and seize enemy flaws, defeating foes through martial arts, and forging your own path with every challenge.

Core Game Content & Features

Martial Arts Card Combat System

Moves include basic and derivative types—derivatives enhance basics, which deal damage and create flaws. Seizing enemy flaws triggers high-damage chain attacks; every round is a tactical battle of move and countermove.

Roguelike Random Dungeon Crawl

Each difficulty has a set number of battles, with customizable challenge order. Choose from multiple rewards after each victory. The game includes permadeath—adventure progress resets on death, ensuring unique playthroughs every time.

In-Run Progression

Move damage scales with character attributes. Win battles to gain attribute upgrades, boosting damage and flaw-creating ability. Use attribute points to increase max health and flaw capacity.

Diverse Items, Moves & Elixirs

Unlock and collect dozens of items, martial arts moves, and elixirs. Flexibly use resources during your journey to create endless combat strategy variations.

The game features substantial content and high replay‑value. This is a buy‑to‑play title with no in‑game purchases, no character voice‑over dialogue, and no paid DLC. Unlock all game content with a single purchase.

Hello everyone, I’m JZ3003, an independent game developer.

For me, creating games is even more fascinating than playing them. The thrill of solving a difficult problem, watching my game evolve from simple prototypes to a vivid world, and connecting with players who share my passion—these moments drive me forward.

As I mentioned earlier, I find "balance" and "original intention" in the concept of martial chivalry—balance is the foundation of this game, while original intention is the principle I adhere to throughout my development journey.

Most importantly, a game must be fun. If it brings you excitement and joy during play, and leaves you with fond memories years later, it proves that my choice to pursue game development has never been wrong.

I hope you can find your own version of "Martial" and "Chivalry" in Card Warrior.

store_data.about_the_game:
MYTHORUNE

A cooperative descent into darkness

Heroes go down into the dark together. Everything else is built around not getting in the way of that.

No level scaling. Floor 40 does not quietly become as hard as you are. The world has a difficulty, and you either meet it or go back and get stronger. This is why a level means something here: an upgrade changes a fight, and a stronger friend joining your game actually helps you. Games that scale to the player hand you a reward and cancel it with the same arithmetic that granted it.

Nothing to buy. No battle pass, no seasons, no cosmetics store, no premium currency. You bought a game.

Play however you can physically sit. Five on one couch. LAN, so a house shares one world. Online with friends anywhere. And mixed, which is the one that usually gets skipped: two people on the sofa and two across the country, in the same party. A party holds six.

Host your own server. One button in the launcher says Open the gates, and your machine becomes the world. Others join by typing an address, from the game or from a browser. No account, no matchmaking service, no dependency on anyone else staying online. If you want a private world for six months for four friends, you have one, and it sits on your hard drive.

The descent

Mythorune is an endless dungeon crawler. Floors run past 250 and keep going.

Each region has its own weather and its own shape: the Widow's Caverns, the Cursed Crypts, the Blighted Mire, the Burning Depths, the Frostbound Halls, and the Flower-Fruit Wilds, where real rivers carve the floors and you cross them at fords. Storms roll across the open floors. Wind moves through grass in fields you can watch bend under it. Water runs as a real wave field, so wakes spread, cross each other and bounce off shores instead of scrolling past as a texture.

Four classes: Barbarian, Wizard, Hunter, Læknan. Even the healer is armed: her mending ray is the same ray that sears the undead, and stone and gale answer her when she is not mending. None of them exists to stand behind the others, and a party of three Wizards is a legitimate party.

Loot runs common, magic, rare, legendary, set, mythic, and RED. Legendaries are not adjectives stapled to a noun. They are named relics out of world myth: Gungnir, Excalibur, the Aegis of Zeus, the Yata no Kagami, Sleipnir's hooves, the Apple of Idunn. Finding one is finding a specific object with a story attached, not a good roll.

Weapons and armour can be bound to beast spirits. Masks carved from what you killed go on your face. Cards cut from monsters socket into gear. Ore dug out of the walls upgrades anything.

The four heroes and their fuel

Six skills each, and they run on four resources that behave nothing alike.

The Wizard burns Seidr, which regenerates on its own. She can stand and pour damage until the bar empties, then wait. The Barbarian runs on Wod, which starts empty, does not regenerate, and only fills when he kills something. He earns his big moves by fighting; standing still gives him nothing. The Hunter uses Veidr, in between, with slow passive regeneration. The Læknan runs on Önd, which returns quickly and asks a different price: her strongest work is a thread, and a thread is a tether she has to stand in.

That difference is most of what separates the classes in a fight. The Wizard opens strong and fades. The Barbarian opens with nothing and gets more dangerous the longer the room lasts. The Hunter has to spend at a rhythm. The Læknan chooses, every second, between mending and striking, because both come out of the same green bar. She is also the only hero whose power splits its books: Faith pays for her healing, Intelligence for her damage.

Skills are named for what they take from: Splinter of Gungnir, Breath of Niflheim, Mjolnir's Fall, Sleipnir's Bound, Skadi's Volley, Shears of the Norns, The Wild Hunt.

Runes rewrite skills

Every skill has three or four rune variants, and a rune does not add a percentage. It changes what the skill is.

Bifrost, the Wizard's channel, is a beam that sears the first enemy it touches and drains Seidr for every second you hold it. Slot Isa and it becomes a lance of pure cold that drains far slower, a beam you hold rather than spend. Slot Kenaz and it becomes a jet of fire, far wider, engulfing everything around the point it strikes. Slot Laguz and it becomes a caustic ray that bores straight through enemies and keeps going.

Same button, four different weapons. Whether you want single-target burst, sustain, an area sweep or a line down a corridor is a build decision, not a menu preference.

Channelled skills have their own economics. Bifrost's reach grows with your level, from a stub at unlock to something that crosses the screen, thickening as it lengthens. It demands a real reserve of resource before it will start at all, then drains until you are empty. You cannot tap it. Committing to a channel means committing.

Loot, and what an affix actually does

Eleven equipment slots: weapon, offhand, cape, head, chest, legs, boots, hands, gauntlets, ring, amulet. Plus a bag slot and a potion slot.

Affixes are the usual attributes (strength, intellect, dexterity, vitality, faith, armour, crit chance, crit damage, attack speed, life, life on hit, movement speed, gold find) and then the ones that shape a build: elemental damage by school, primary and secondary attack damage, and per-class skill damage. A wizard-damage roll on a ring is worthless to the Hunter standing next to you, which is what makes trading inside a party worth doing.

Rarity runs common, magic, rare, legendary, set, mythic, RED. The number of affixes climbs with rarity, and so does a damage multiplier, but RED sits outside the ladder: it multiplies again on top of mythic.

Items arrive unidentified. You can read base damage and armour, which is enough to weigh whether a relic is worth the fee, but the affixes and the real name stay hidden until Auric appraises it. The veil is enforced on the server rather than in the interface, so the secrets are not sitting in the page waiting to be read.

Bags, potions, ore, cards

Bags take a slot and add inventory cells. A worn sack carries a few. A void cache carries far more. Space is a stat you equip.

Potions heal a percentage and, from rare upward, carry a buff: speed, haste, damage, resource, or invulnerability. A RED potion is the only one with more than one, and always includes an invulnerability window.

Ore comes out of the walls, once breakable walls are switched on in the options. You mine it, it stacks by rarity, and it upgrades gear of that rarity. There is one grade per tier, up to Starfall Ore, which is the only thing that will lift a mythic.

Cards drop from monsters and socket into gear that has a card slot. Card slot punches cut another slot into a piece, up to five. A well-slotted rare can outlive a legendary you found later.

Beast spirits bind to gear and chain, so several sworn pieces compound. The binding is read out of the item's name, so a spirit-sworn relic announces itself.

Floors, and what is in them

Floors are generated rather than authored, and the deep ones are larger and more tangled than the shallow ones. You find the stairs, or you don't, and the minimap flags them once a floor has been picked over. Floors restock out of sight, so a level you cleared an hour ago is not empty when you come back through it.

Walls are breakable. Some are ordinary rock hiding ore, some are cracked plugs sealing shortcuts and back chambers, and mining changes the shape of the floor you are standing in.

Boss floors are one enormous arena cut into the maze, and the arena keeps widening with depth. During a boss round the bosses are marked purple on the minimap regardless of what you have explored, because hunting a boss around a floor is not the interesting part of a boss.

Death is counted against the party rather than the individual. Enough of them and the dark casts everyone back.

Playing together

Six can share one world, and the party genuinely mixes: couch players in one room, LAN players in the house, online friends anywhere, all at once.

Party voice runs push-to-talk on a key you choose.

The strongbox is shared storage, and it is Auric's cache. Everything you deposit sits in a raven's hoard, which is a joke the game does not explain until much later.

Story

You are dreaming, and at some point you realise it.

Then you wake up. Then you wake up again. A run of false awakenings, each one convincing right up until it isn't. Eventually you wake in your own room, except the room is faded and drowned in purple static, and something is calling you.

It is a raven.

On the shelf in that room is one object from every culture you just dreamt. Each is a gift from a friend, and each has a story behind it. That shelf is the only exposition the opening gives you, and it quietly answers a question you would otherwise never think to ask: why these six worlds? Because you know people there.

The raven is Auric, a spirit guide who travels mythology itself. Not the astral plane, but the substrate the gods are made of, where Wukong's mountain and Kaliya's poisoned river and the eclipse that swallows the sun are less separate worlds than separate rooms of one sleeping mind. He caught you projecting. He was impressed. He would like your help.

What he wants is runes, and the alphabet is the point. Elder Futhark is your language, not the pantheon's. The gods you meet are Chinese, Japanese, Hindu, Norse and Filipino, and they owe each other nothing. A rune is how you write down what you took from one of them. That is why a monkey god and a world serpent can share a game without either being flattened into the other: they were never meant to be the same tradition. The runes are your record, not their religion.

So you go down. Six realms, six guardians, six powers written into six letters. Auric is on every floor, cheerful, useful, and never fighting.

Spoilers

Everything below gives away the plot, including the ending. Stop here if you would rather find it.

Auric is the weaker party, and that is the whole character. He cannot fight gods, which is exactly why you exist to him. He can only reach people who project the way you do, and those people are always better than him. He does not take; he receives. His charm is not power, it is compensation. He flatters because he cannot compel, and jokes because wit is the only leverage he has ever had. His engine is envy rather than ambition, which is more pathetic than a mastermind and more dangerous in one specific way: desperate things move first.

His name has been telling you the whole time. Auric means of gold, and gold is useless. Too soft for a blade or a tool, good only for decorating or hoarding. The wolf who opposes him is Ferric, of iron: common, dull, strong, everywhere. Nobody hoards iron. You make things out of it.

The raven and the wolf are not a tidy symmetry. They are a real relationship. Ravens follow wolves, and are called wolf-birds for it. A raven can find a carcass but cannot open one, because its beak will not tear hide. So it calls the wolves in and eats what their jaws open. The first sound in the game is a bird calling a predator toward a kill. None of that is metaphor.

The objects on your shelf are doorways. Six friends, six gifts, six roads, which is how you reach six realms at all, and why Auric has none of his own. He has no bonds, so he has never had a door. What he hoards is roads, not trinkets.

That makes his theft something worse than burglary. Take the doorway and you can never reach that friend again. He does not take a keepsake, he takes the person. And once he holds the only road to someone, he is the only thing left that can wear their face. The transformation is not a trick he performs. It is what remains of them.

He is also a god eater. He gains the power of every rune you take, at the moment you take it. You are not his employee, you are his hands. Six gods robbed on his behalf is not six errands. It is six meals.

Which makes the ending close cleanly. He arrives holding your six runes, and someone wielding your borrowed power cannot exceed you. He can only ever be you, secondhand, losing to the person he borrowed it from.

MYTHORUNE

A cooperative descent into darkness

Heroes go down into the dark together. Everything else is built around not getting in the way of that.

No level scaling. Floor 40 does not quietly become as hard as you are. The world has a difficulty, and you either meet it or go back and get stronger. This is why a level means something here: an upgrade changes a fight, and a stronger friend joining your game actually helps you. Games that scale to the player hand you a reward and cancel it with the same arithmetic that granted it.

Nothing to buy. No battle pass, no seasons, no cosmetics store, no premium currency. You bought a game.

Play however you can physically sit. Five on one couch. LAN, so a house shares one world. Online with friends anywhere. And mixed, which is the one that usually gets skipped: two people on the sofa and two across the country, in the same party. A party holds six.

Host your own server. One button in the launcher says Open the gates, and your machine becomes the world. Others join by typing an address, from the game or from a browser. No account, no matchmaking service, no dependency on anyone else staying online. If you want a private world for six months for four friends, you have one, and it sits on your hard drive.

The descent

Mythorune is an endless dungeon crawler. Floors run past 250 and keep going.

Each region has its own weather and its own shape: the Widow's Caverns, the Cursed Crypts, the Blighted Mire, the Burning Depths, the Frostbound Halls, and the Flower-Fruit Wilds, where real rivers carve the floors and you cross them at fords. Storms roll across the open floors. Wind moves through grass in fields you can watch bend under it. Water runs as a real wave field, so wakes spread, cross each other and bounce off shores instead of scrolling past as a texture.

Four classes: Barbarian, Wizard, Hunter, Læknan. Even the healer is armed: her mending ray is the same ray that sears the undead, and stone and gale answer her when she is not mending. None of them exists to stand behind the others, and a party of three Wizards is a legitimate party.

Loot runs common, magic, rare, legendary, set, mythic, and RED. Legendaries are not adjectives stapled to a noun. They are named relics out of world myth: Gungnir, Excalibur, the Aegis of Zeus, the Yata no Kagami, Sleipnir's hooves, the Apple of Idunn. Finding one is finding a specific object with a story attached, not a good roll.

Weapons and armour can be bound to beast spirits. Masks carved from what you killed go on your face. Cards cut from monsters socket into gear. Ore dug out of the walls upgrades anything.

The four heroes and their fuel

Six skills each, and they run on four resources that behave nothing alike.

The Wizard burns Seidr, which regenerates on its own. She can stand and pour damage until the bar empties, then wait. The Barbarian runs on Wod, which starts empty, does not regenerate, and only fills when he kills something. He earns his big moves by fighting; standing still gives him nothing. The Hunter uses Veidr, in between, with slow passive regeneration. The Læknan runs on Önd, which returns quickly and asks a different price: her strongest work is a thread, and a thread is a tether she has to stand in.

That difference is most of what separates the classes in a fight. The Wizard opens strong and fades. The Barbarian opens with nothing and gets more dangerous the longer the room lasts. The Hunter has to spend at a rhythm. The Læknan chooses, every second, between mending and striking, because both come out of the same green bar. She is also the only hero whose power splits its books: Faith pays for her healing, Intelligence for her damage.

Skills are named for what they take from: Splinter of Gungnir, Breath of Niflheim, Mjolnir's Fall, Sleipnir's Bound, Skadi's Volley, Shears of the Norns, The Wild Hunt.

Runes rewrite skills

Every skill has three or four rune variants, and a rune does not add a percentage. It changes what the skill is.

Bifrost, the Wizard's channel, is a beam that sears the first enemy it touches and drains Seidr for every second you hold it. Slot Isa and it becomes a lance of pure cold that drains far slower, a beam you hold rather than spend. Slot Kenaz and it becomes a jet of fire, far wider, engulfing everything around the point it strikes. Slot Laguz and it becomes a caustic ray that bores straight through enemies and keeps going.

Same button, four different weapons. Whether you want single-target burst, sustain, an area sweep or a line down a corridor is a build decision, not a menu preference.

Channelled skills have their own economics. Bifrost's reach grows with your level, from a stub at unlock to something that crosses the screen, thickening as it lengthens. It demands a real reserve of resource before it will start at all, then drains until you are empty. You cannot tap it. Committing to a channel means committing.

Loot, and what an affix actually does

Eleven equipment slots: weapon, offhand, cape, head, chest, legs, boots, hands, gauntlets, ring, amulet. Plus a bag slot and a potion slot.

Affixes are the usual attributes (strength, intellect, dexterity, vitality, faith, armour, crit chance, crit damage, attack speed, life, life on hit, movement speed, gold find) and then the ones that shape a build: elemental damage by school, primary and secondary attack damage, and per-class skill damage. A wizard-damage roll on a ring is worthless to the Hunter standing next to you, which is what makes trading inside a party worth doing.

Rarity runs common, magic, rare, legendary, set, mythic, RED. The number of affixes climbs with rarity, and so does a damage multiplier, but RED sits outside the ladder: it multiplies again on top of mythic.

Items arrive unidentified. You can read base damage and armour, which is enough to weigh whether a relic is worth the fee, but the affixes and the real name stay hidden until Auric appraises it. The veil is enforced on the server rather than in the interface, so the secrets are not sitting in the page waiting to be read.

Bags, potions, ore, cards

Bags take a slot and add inventory cells. A worn sack carries a few. A void cache carries far more. Space is a stat you equip.

Potions heal a percentage and, from rare upward, carry a buff: speed, haste, damage, resource, or invulnerability. A RED potion is the only one with more than one, and always includes an invulnerability window.

Ore comes out of the walls, once breakable walls are switched on in the options. You mine it, it stacks by rarity, and it upgrades gear of that rarity. There is one grade per tier, up to Starfall Ore, which is the only thing that will lift a mythic.

Cards drop from monsters and socket into gear that has a card slot. Card slot punches cut another slot into a piece, up to five. A well-slotted rare can outlive a legendary you found later.

Beast spirits bind to gear and chain, so several sworn pieces compound. The binding is read out of the item's name, so a spirit-sworn relic announces itself.

Floors, and what is in them

Floors are generated rather than authored, and the deep ones are larger and more tangled than the shallow ones. You find the stairs, or you don't, and the minimap flags them once a floor has been picked over. Floors restock out of sight, so a level you cleared an hour ago is not empty when you come back through it.

Walls are breakable. Some are ordinary rock hiding ore, some are cracked plugs sealing shortcuts and back chambers, and mining changes the shape of the floor you are standing in.

Boss floors are one enormous arena cut into the maze, and the arena keeps widening with depth. During a boss round the bosses are marked purple on the minimap regardless of what you have explored, because hunting a boss around a floor is not the interesting part of a boss.

Death is counted against the party rather than the individual. Enough of them and the dark casts everyone back.

Playing together

Six can share one world, and the party genuinely mixes: couch players in one room, LAN players in the house, online friends anywhere, all at once.

Party voice runs push-to-talk on a key you choose.

The strongbox is shared storage, and it is Auric's cache. Everything you deposit sits in a raven's hoard, which is a joke the game does not explain until much later.

Story

You are dreaming, and at some point you realise it.

Then you wake up. Then you wake up again. A run of false awakenings, each one convincing right up until it isn't. Eventually you wake in your own room, except the room is faded and drowned in purple static, and something is calling you.

It is a raven.

On the shelf in that room is one object from every culture you just dreamt. Each is a gift from a friend, and each has a story behind it. That shelf is the only exposition the opening gives you, and it quietly answers a question you would otherwise never think to ask: why these six worlds? Because you know people there.

The raven is Auric, a spirit guide who travels mythology itself. Not the astral plane, but the substrate the gods are made of, where Wukong's mountain and Kaliya's poisoned river and the eclipse that swallows the sun are less separate worlds than separate rooms of one sleeping mind. He caught you projecting. He was impressed. He would like your help.

What he wants is runes, and the alphabet is the point. Elder Futhark is your language, not the pantheon's. The gods you meet are Chinese, Japanese, Hindu, Norse and Filipino, and they owe each other nothing. A rune is how you write down what you took from one of them. That is why a monkey god and a world serpent can share a game without either being flattened into the other: they were never meant to be the same tradition. The runes are your record, not their religion.

So you go down. Six realms, six guardians, six powers written into six letters. Auric is on every floor, cheerful, useful, and never fighting.

Spoilers

Everything below gives away the plot, including the ending. Stop here if you would rather find it.

Auric is the weaker party, and that is the whole character. He cannot fight gods, which is exactly why you exist to him. He can only reach people who project the way you do, and those people are always better than him. He does not take; he receives. His charm is not power, it is compensation. He flatters because he cannot compel, and jokes because wit is the only leverage he has ever had. His engine is envy rather than ambition, which is more pathetic than a mastermind and more dangerous in one specific way: desperate things move first.

His name has been telling you the whole time. Auric means of gold, and gold is useless. Too soft for a blade or a tool, good only for decorating or hoarding. The wolf who opposes him is Ferric, of iron: common, dull, strong, everywhere. Nobody hoards iron. You make things out of it.

The raven and the wolf are not a tidy symmetry. They are a real relationship. Ravens follow wolves, and are called wolf-birds for it. A raven can find a carcass but cannot open one, because its beak will not tear hide. So it calls the wolves in and eats what their jaws open. The first sound in the game is a bird calling a predator toward a kill. None of that is metaphor.

The objects on your shelf are doorways. Six friends, six gifts, six roads, which is how you reach six realms at all, and why Auric has none of his own. He has no bonds, so he has never had a door. What he hoards is roads, not trinkets.

That makes his theft something worse than burglary. Take the doorway and you can never reach that friend again. He does not take a keepsake, he takes the person. And once he holds the only road to someone, he is the only thing left that can wear their face. The transformation is not a trick he performs. It is what remains of them.

He is also a god eater. He gains the power of every rune you take, at the moment you take it. You are not his employee, you are his hands. Six gods robbed on his behalf is not six errands. It is six meals.

Which makes the ending close cleanly. He arrives holding your six runes, and someone wielding your borrowed power cannot exceed you. He can only ever be you, secondhand, losing to the person he borrowed it from.
store_data.short_description: An endless co-op action-RPG dungeon crawl. Descend floors that never scale to you, slot runes that rewrite your skills into new weapons, mine the walls, and loot relics of world myth. Play couch, LAN and online in one six-hero party, or host your own server. No microtransactions.

store_data.about_the_game:
Rulebound is a surreal horror incremental game where your survival depends on split attention.

You wake up trapped in a cold, quiet bedroom suspended between reality and the Void. In front of you sits an old CRT TV displaying a strangely hypnotic game. By managing points, merging discs, and buying upgrades, you can forge 3 Golden Discs to escape. 

The problem? You are being observed.

  • Watch’em Bounce: Every border hit earns points; every corner hit triggers massive bonuses.

  • Merge & Multiply: Merge 3 discs to unlock higher tiers and massive score multipliers.

  • Break the Game: Execute secret cheat codes, buy permanent upgrades, and fill your fast-forward bar to push your points into the billions.

  • Stay Focused: Manage the discs while watching for subtle changes as the Void slowly invades your reality.

  • Follow the rules to survive: Use handwritten instructions to detect and fix anomalies before they drain your sanity.

  • Find your way out: Master the strange game inside the CRT TV and uncover the path to escape.

  • Disc-merging incremental game inside a CRT TV.

  • Follow strict room rules, fix environmental anomalies, and survive entity intrusions before your sanity collapses.

  • Discover in-game artwork crafted by various artists, viewable anytime in Gallery Mode.

  • Secret cheat codes.

store_data.about_the_game:
Cartoon Crime is an open-world action game built around freedom, exploration, street fights, and the kind of chaos that happens when you stop following the objective marker.

Explore the city at your own pace, take on missions, make money, buy weapons, improve your skills, recruit bodyguards, and find new things to do across the map. You can follow the story, spend time building up your character, or simply head into the streets and see where the day takes you.

Switch freely between third-person and a classic top-down camera while playing. Third-person brings you closer to the action, while the overhead view gives the game a more old-school arcade crime-game feel.

The world is designed to be more than scenery. You can enter different shops and interiors, visit gun stores, work out at gyms, eat at fast-food restaurants, watch movies at cinemas, play bowling and billiards, use arcade machines, and discover activities scattered around the cities.

Combat is not limited to guns. Get into fist fights, use kicks and melee weapons, improve your fighting ability, and take part in kickboxing challenges against increasingly dangerous opponents. Different skills improve as you play, giving you more reasons to explore activities beyond the main missions.

The streets react to what you do. Start trouble and civilians may run, fight back, or get caught in the chaos. Push things further and the police become involved. As your wanted level increases, escaping becomes harder and the situation can quickly turn into a full chase.

You can also recruit bodyguards who follow you around the city and fight alongside you when things get dangerous.

Features

  • Open-world action with missions and free-roam sandbox gameplay

  • Multiple cities, districts, islands, and locations to explore

  • Instant switching between third-person and top-down views

  • Enterable shops, gun stores, gyms, cinemas, restaurants, and other interiors

  • Kickboxing rings with different fighters, difficulty levels, and cash rewards

  • Fist fighting, kicks, melee weapons, firearms, and different combat styles

  • Character skills that improve through gameplay and activities

  • Recruitable bodyguards who follow and protect you

  • Police pursuits with escalating wanted levels

  • Rival gangs and hostile NPC encounters

  • Bowling, billiards, arcade machines, cinema visits, and other side activities

  • Bicycles and different vehicles to use around the world

  • Multiple playable characters

  • Multiple difficulty settings

  • A city where civilians can react differently to fights and trouble

  • Freedom to follow the story or completely ignore it and create your own chaos

Take missions, train your character, challenge fighters, explore interiors, build your crew, cause trouble, or just spend time around the city.

Cartoon Crime gives you a world to play with, not just a list of missions to complete.

store_data.about_the_game:
Wordgeon is a roguelike deckbuilder where you fight with spelling and vocabulary.

How to play

  • Build your deck from word cards. Spell and translate words to deal damage to dungeon monsters.

  • Buy relics and combine them with your cards to multiply your damage.

  • Stamp word cards to smooth out your draws and make your relics work even better.

Strategic Depth

  • 150+ relics

  • 15+ stamp types for word cards

  • 20+ enemy traits

Every run asks you to find a different combo. No two runs play the same.

Learn while you play

  • Choose from difficulty levels vocabulary lists across multiple languages.

  • Or add your own custom word lists.

  • You’ll pick up new words naturally as you play.

※ Add it to your Wishlist!

Hello, I'm an independent game developer.

If you enjoy cute dogs, warm companionship, and a relaxing desktop experience, please consider adding this game to your wishlist.

Your support is the best way to help me continue creating this little companion game.

1. Raise your dog and let it accompany your daily life

Have you ever imagined this?

When you turn on your computer, a little dog is waiting for you on your desktop.

It will live alongside you, accompanying you while you work, study, or relax.

You can pet it, play with it, and spend quiet moments together.

It is not just a tool, but a little companion that stays by your side.

2. Features

a. Raise a dog that is uniquely yours

▪ Choose dogs with different appearances and characteristics, and collect accessories to personalize them.

▪ Watch your dog grow from a little puppy into a lifelong companion.

b. Decorate its little home

▪ Purchase different beds, toys, and decorations.

▪ Create a comfortable space just for your dog.

▪ Build a unique desktop corner based on your own style.

c. A relaxing idle experience

▪ The game quietly runs on your desktop.

▪ No complicated controls and no stressful tasks.

▪ Every time you turn on your computer, your familiar companion will be there.

d. A warm pixel-art world

▪ Hand-crafted pixel animations.

▪ Charming little behaviors and adorable interactions.

▪ Record the everyday moments you spend with your dog through simple and heartwarming visuals.

※ More items and decorations will continue to be added in future updates.

store_data.about_the_game:
About Across the Dungeon

Only strategy, synergy, and your sharp intellect will keep you alive.

[Across the Dungeon] is a dark fantasy roguelike deckbuilder that pushes strategic planning and meaningful choices to their absolute limit.

Fight your way through 5 brutal stages to reach the 6th and final stage, where the Demon Lord awaits in the deepest depths. In a unforgiving journey where a single death resets all your progress, how far will your strategy take you?

KEY FEATURES

4 Distinct Classes with Unique Mechanics

Bloodslayer / IronGuard / GrandMage / SwiftHealer

Choose from 4 distinct heroes, each featuring unique combat tactics and card synergies. Maximize your class's strengths or buy items from other classes to create unpredictable, game-breaking synergies.

8 Card Slots & Strategic Synergies

Battle outcomes hinge entirely on how you arrange cards and equipment across your 8 limited slots. Calculate intricate links between gear and cards to discover the ultimate combination that shuts down enemy attacks.

Automated Combat: Strategy Over Reflexes

No fast reflexes or intense physical execution required. Your main tasks are meticulous health management and flawless deck construction. Sit back and watch your carefully crafted setup overpower every foe in battle.

3 Specialized Shops: Strategic Resource Management

Spend the limited currency earned from defeating monsters wisely by choosing which shop to visit:

Item Shop: Acquire class-specific gear, cross-class items, and powerful relics to complete your deck.

Forge (Upgrade Shop): Push your favorite key items to their maximum potential.

Skill Shop: Once your item build is set, equip game-changing skills to turn the tide of battle.

Deciding where to invest your hard-earned resources is the true key to survival.

Game-Changing Random Events

Encounter unpredictable events as you venture deeper into the dungeon. A split-second decision can bring great fortune—or prove fatal. Every choice you make reshapes the fate of your run.

5 Brutal Stages & The Final Showdown

Overcome 5 increasingly lethal stages filled with complex enemy attack patterns. Only those who master every challenge will earn the right to face the ultimate boss in the 6th stage.

One life. 8 slots. Infinite strategies.

Enter the deadly yet captivating depths of Across the Dungeon today!

store_data.about_the_game:
Every abandoned town has a story.

This one has something waiting.

Project Potato Man: Chapter 1 is a first-person psychological horror game where exploration, atmosphere, and constant tension take center stage. Step into a forgotten town consumed by darkness, where empty streets, abandoned buildings, and unsettling silence hide an unimaginable nightmare.

As you explore, you'll slowly uncover clues about the town's mysterious past while a terrifying entity known only as Potato Man relentlessly stalks your every move. Sometimes you'll hear it. Sometimes you'll see it.

Sometimes it's already behind you.

Unlike traditional horror games that rely only on cheap jump scares, Project Potato Man builds fear through immersive environments, disturbing audio, and the feeling that you're never truly alone.

Every location has been carefully crafted to create suspense—from deserted streets and abandoned homes to narrow alleys swallowed by darkness. Your flashlight may guide your path, but it won't make you feel safe.

This is only the beginning of a much larger story.

Will you survive long enough to discover the truth?

Over rafted! is a co-op multiplayer game for up to four players, where you navigate a raft across an endless ocean. Share the workload as you steer, fish, gather supplies, and make repairs—and keep your raft from falling apart when no one is looking!

No two voyages go according to plan! Shifting winds and currents, treacherous waters, volcanic eruptions, and all kinds of sea creatures will turn life aboard your raft into chaos. Communicate with your crew and work together to overcome one disaster after another.

Your food supply will slowly run out as you sail. Catch fish to keep hunger at bay, gather materials drifting across the ocean, and repair your battered raft. Deciding who steers, who finds food, and who gathers supplies is the key to survival—and those roles may need to change at a moment’s notice.

Reach a port, and you can use the materials you have collected to upgrade your raft and equipment. Expanding your raft gives your crew more options, but it also leaves you with more to protect. Join forces with your friends, venture into an ever-changing ocean, and see how far your crew can make it!

store_data.about_the_game:
UNLISTED

UNLISTED is a multiplayer social horror game set inside an underground containment facility where something has gone terribly wrong.

You and the other survivors must restore the facility, gather essential supplies, investigate abnormal activity, and find a way out.

The problem is simple.

Not everyone is human.

Something inside the facility can imitate one of you.

Work together to restore power, access restricted areas, recover critical equipment, and complete the tasks required for escape. But every time the group splits up, every unexplained disappearance, and every suspicious action gives you another reason to doubt the people around you.

Communication is essential—but so is knowing when not to trust what you hear.

Trust No One

The greatest threat may already be standing beside you.

A hostile mimic hides among the survivors, appearing human until it decides to reveal its true nature. It can exploit isolated players, disrupted systems, and moments of confusion to break the group apart.

Pay attention to where people have been, what they claim to have seen, and whether their story makes sense.

Accusing the wrong person can be just as dangerous as trusting the right one.

Keep the Facility Running

The containment facility is failing around you.

Restore damaged systems, reactivate equipment, search storage areas for supplies, and gain access to restricted sections of the complex.

Important tasks may require players to separate or cooperate in different parts of the facility, creating opportunities for both teamwork and betrayal.

Power failures, locked areas, communication problems, and abnormal events can quickly turn a simple objective into a crisis.

Communication Is Part of Survival

Talk with the people around you.

Share information, coordinate tasks, call for help—or lie.

Voice communication plays an important role in determining who can be trusted. When players disappear around a corner or enter another section of the facility, you may have to decide whether their explanation is believable.

Sometimes the most dangerous thing you can hear is a familiar voice.

Key Features

  • 6–8 Player Multiplayer Social Horror

  • Hidden roles and player deception

  • A hostile creature capable of hiding among the group

  • Proximity-based player communication

  • Cooperative facility objectives

  • Power, security, communication, medical, and containment systems

  • Weapons and limited survival equipment

  • Dynamic situations created by player decisions

  • A compact facility designed around encounters, suspicion, and separation

  • Different stories every round depending on who you decide to trust

Restore the facility.

Find a way out.

And before you trust the person standing next to you—

make sure they are still human.

store_data.about_the_game:
BUILD A COLONY, ONE BLOCK AT A TIME

StoneEra is an isometric voxel colony simulation where you build, manage, and expand a medieval settlement in a fully editable procedural world.

Gather resources, assign villagers to specialized professions, organize production, and reshape the terrain as your small camp grows into a thriving colony. Every block can be mined, placed, or transformed—and every decision leaves a permanent mark on the world.

BUILD AND MANAGE YOUR SETTLEMENT

Start with the essentials, then expand according to the needs of your people. Construct buildings, process raw materials, plan efficient production chains, and decide which projects deserve priority.

Your villagers work as builders, miners, farmers, woodcutters, and other specialists. Assign the right people to the right jobs and keep resources moving as your population grows.

EXPLORE A LIVING PROCEDURAL WORLD

Every new game creates a different voxel landscape filled with forests, mountains, rivers, caves, distinct biomes, and valuable resources.

Day turns into night, weather changes, and the seasons transform the land around your colony. Explore to find fertile farmland, strategic building locations, and the resources your settlement needs to survive and expand.

RESHAPE THE LAND

The world is more than scenery—it is yours to transform. Mine through mountains, dig underground, redirect your expansion around natural obstacles, or rebuild the landscape block by block.

Build with the terrain or redesign it completely. Your colony develops according to your plans, priorities, and creativity.

PLAN, PRODUCE, AND GROW

A successful colony depends on careful resource management. Farming feeds your people, woodcutting supplies construction materials, mining reveals underground resources, and crafting turns raw materials into useful goods.

Balance immediate needs with long-term growth while changing seasons and weather challenge your plans.

KEY FEATURES

  • Build and manage a medieval voxel colony

  • Explore procedurally generated worlds

  • Mine, place, and reshape terrain block by block

  • Manage AI-controlled villagers with specialized professions

  • Organize resource gathering, crafting, and production chains

  • Discover forests, rivers, mountains, caves, and diverse biomes

  • Experience dynamic seasons, weather, and a full day/night cycle

  • Save your colony and continue developing it over time

  • Play at your own pace in a single-player sandbox simulation

LEAVE YOUR MARK ON THE LAND

store_data.detailed_description:
BUILD A COLONY, ONE BLOCK AT A TIME

StoneEra is an isometric voxel colony simulation where you build, manage, and expand a medieval settlement in a fully editable procedural world.

Gather resources, assign villagers to specialized professions, organize production, and reshape the terrain as your small camp grows into a thriving colony. Every block can be mined, placed, or transformed—and every decision leaves a permanent mark on the world.

BUILD AND MANAGE YOUR SETTLEMENT

Start with the essentials, then expand according to the needs of your people. Construct buildings, process raw materials, plan efficient production chains, and decide which projects deserve priority.

Your villagers work as builders, miners, farmers, woodcutters, and other specialists. Assign the right people to the right jobs and keep resources moving as your population grows.

EXPLORE A LIVING PROCEDURAL WORLD

Every new game creates a different voxel landscape filled with forests, mountains, rivers, caves, distinct biomes, and valuable resources.

Day turns into night, weather changes, and the seasons transform the land around your colony. Explore to find fertile farmland, strategic building locations, and the resources your settlement needs to survive and expand.

RESHAPE THE LAND

The world is more than scenery—it is yours to transform. Mine through mountains, dig underground, redirect your expansion around natural obstacles, or rebuild the landscape block by block.

Build with the terrain or redesign it completely. Your colony develops according to your plans, priorities, and creativity.

PLAN, PRODUCE, AND GROW

A successful colony depends on careful resource management. Farming feeds your people, woodcutting supplies construction materials, mining reveals underground resources, and crafting turns raw materials into useful goods.

Balance immediate needs with long-term growth while changing seasons and weather challenge your plans.

KEY FEATURES

  • Build and manage a medieval voxel colony

  • Explore procedurally generated worlds

  • Mine, place, and reshape terrain block by block

  • Manage AI-controlled villagers with specialized professions

  • Organize resource gathering, crafting, and production chains

  • Discover forests, rivers, mountains, caves, and diverse biomes

  • Experience dynamic seasons, weather, and a full day/night cycle

  • Save your colony and continue developing it over time

  • Play at your own pace in a single-player sandbox simulation

LEAVE YOUR MARK ON THE LAND

Every colony tells a different story. Work with the landscape or reshape it entirely, organize your people, and build a settlement that reflects your decisions.

Wishlist StoneEra and follow its development.

Lead your people away from persecution and settle in an unknown wilderness to build a new home. In this harsh land filled with danger and opportunity, you must establish your settlement from nothing, develop production, manage resources, and protect your people from outside threats.

Build shelters, cultivate land, develop industries, and recruit new settlers as a small refuge grows into a powerful domain. As your influence expands, you will face invaders, rival forces, and countless challenges hidden across the wilderness.

Your lord is not just a figure behind a management screen, but a living character within the world. Your lord can independently work, fight, and explore alongside your people. While exploring the world, you will encounter dynamic events: welcoming refugees, discovering hidden enemies, facing bandit attacks, or finding opportunities that could change the fate of your settlement. Every decision you make will shape the future of your new homeland.

Build your settlement, protect your people, explore the unknown, and create your own legend as a lord.

store_data.about_the_game:
Enter the Memory Library

The Akashic Archives preserve countless memories and forgotten stories. But after the mysterious “Incursion of Oblivion,” corrupted records begin transforming into monsters.

As a newly appointed Archivist, you must enter these damaged records, defeat the creatures within, and recover the memories that are being erased.

Customize Your Card Artwork

Freely replace card artwork with image files stored on your computer. If the default artwork is difficult to recognize or does not suit your preferences, use images that are easier for you to identify and manage your deck your way.

Build Your Deck

Create a deck that fits your strategy and adapt it throughout each expedition. Discover new cards, strengthen your deck, and combine cards through synthesis to create more powerful options.

Every turn matters. Balance offense, defense, resources, potions, and card combinations to survive increasingly dangerous battles.

Choose Your Class

Play as distinct classes, including the Warrior, Rogue, and Mage. Each class offers its own cards, traits, and combat style, allowing you to approach every run differently.

Unlock and equip traits to shape your character’s growth and create specialized builds.

Prepare Between Expeditions

Return to the Library between journeys to:

  • Build and manage your decks

  • Purchase card packs and potions

  • Synthesize and upgrade cards

  • Unlock and equip permanent traits

  • Review discovered cards, monsters, potions, and recipes

Explore Ten Chapters

Journey through ten story chapters filled with battles, events, powerful enemies, and fragments of forgotten memories. Make choices, improve your build, and uncover the truth behind the Archives and the Incursion of Oblivion.

Challenge the Endless Dungeon

After mastering the main journey, test your strongest builds in the Endless Dungeon. Choose between Short and Full modes, push deeper through consecutive records, and compete against your own best scores and previous runs.

store_data.about_the_game:
Enjoy a clean, relaxing Mahjong Solitaire game built for quick sessions and thoughtful puzzle play.

Match open pairs of beautifully illustrated Mahjong tiles, clear the board, and explore a large collection of classic tile layouts. Mahjong Solitaire is easy to learn: choose two matching free tiles, remove them from the board, and keep going until every tile is cleared.

Features:

Classic Mahjong Solitaire tile matching

84 board layouts inspired by traditional solitaire patterns

Readable Riichi-style Mahjong tile artwork

Random layout mode for fresh puzzles

Hints when you want a nudge

Undo support for relaxed play

Shuffle mode for easier games

Expert mode for a tougher challenge

Timer, best time, and win-loss records

Calm themes and tabletop backgrounds

Autosave so you can resume your board later

Whether you know it as Mahjong Solitaire, Shanghai solitaire, mahjongg, or a classic tile matching puzzle, this game is designed to be calm, clear, and satisfying. The interface stays focused on the board, with large readable tiles, simple controls, and no clutter.

Play a relaxing puzzle when you have a few minutes, chase a faster clear time, or try expert mode and solve without hints or undo. Every board is a small strategy challenge: look ahead, uncover hidden stacks, and avoid blocking matching pairs.

Mahjong Solitaire is perfect for players who enjoy matching games, logic puzzles, classic board games, and quiet brain training.

store_data.about_the_game:
Democracy Simulator's flagship feature is it's intricately designed electoral and economic simulations, which respond to your decisions and policies! Each law you pass, budget you submit, and event you respond to will all affect the simulation! Economic policies will affect metrics like economic growth, which will in turn affect how voters feel about re-electing your party in the next election!

However, you won't be put into power immediately. Instead, you'll have to campaign for the premiership and form a coalition government with other parties! Keep your partners happy or they might propose a vote of no confidence and remove you from power! In a few years, you'll have to defend your majority in another election, with no guarantee of success. If you lose, though, you may still be invited to join the government. If you have enough seats, you can even play kingmaker and help decide who becomes Prime Minister! If not, perhaps you'll plot your comeback from the opposition benches...

Any party with at least one seat can propose legislation. Many laws can be customized with various options and up to 3 can be packaged into a single bill to get other parties to back something you want in exchange for something they want! Laws require a majority to pass, which means you'll often rely on other parties. Once adopted, laws will have effects on the simulation, including electoral boosts or penalties, economic ramifications, and more! Like in real life, you'll have to balance the trade offs and determine what the effects are by watching economic and political metrics.

Occasionally, events will occur that you'll need to respond to. Usually, the Prime Minister is the one calling the shots. You'll be presented with a few options and must decide on one of them. Your choice will affect the simulation and if you pledge to change a law, the voters will remember whether you fulfilled your promise! Democracy Simulator doesn't hold your hand and tell you which option is the most optimal, so you'll have to make your own decision with the information available to you.

The vanilla base game has 2 decades of story events that will drive the narrative and impact the simulation! Economic recessions, geopolitical schenanigans, and political shakeups will ensue! In some cases, you'll be able to affect the story. Some events will appear at random, but the chance may be affected by certain conditions, like legislation or the economy. Others will always occur if their conditions are met.

Do you want to lead your country to prosperity, bask in the chaos, or just see what would happen? A simulated world awaits!

store_data.about_the_game:
Plot

After awakening in a mysterious clocktower, Chime must solve puzzles and answer riddles to find her way out of the labyrinthian dreamscape, floor by floor. The environment is familiar to her, but she's not quite sure why.

Unique Gameplay

Curse of the Countess features a unique blend of Sokoban (block pushing) mechanics, rhythmic projectile-shooting enemies, environmental puzzles and a moody, atmospheric story, all culminating into an experience unlike any other. Pensive, charming, and ponderous.

Doomsday Clock

Reminiscent of games like Majoras Mask, Curse of the Countess features a counter that consistently ticks downward, driving the player forward and forcing concise decision-making in a world full of mystery.

Features

  • 6 Main floors to navigate, each with their own sets of obstacles

  • Environmental puzzles with hidden within the broader landscape

  • Hidden pathways and secrets

  • A variety of riddles and puzzles, ranging in complexity

  • Engaging boss fights that test the players understanding of the world

  • Classic visuals nodding to the PSX era with a complimentary art style

Game Length

A standard run is expected to take between 2-3 hours with enough procedural generation and RNG to allow for satisfying replayability.

Generative AI

We use absolutely no generative AI assets, (or store-bought assets) in this game.
Curse of the Countess is entirely handcrafted.

store_data.about_the_game:
The moment you make a sound, the seeker will find you.

BLINDFOLD: Sound Chase is an asymmetric online hide-and-seek game in which one blindfolded seeker faces a group of fugitives.

The seeker cannot rely on normal vision. Instead, they must follow footsteps, echoes, and other sounds to track down the fugitives.

The fugitives can see their surroundings, but every movement risks revealing their location. Decide whether to run, move quietly, or hold your breath and wait for the seeker to pass.

Track Them Through Sound

For the seeker, sound is more important than sight.

Listen carefully to footsteps and noises coming from the environment. Estimate their direction, follow the trail, and close in on the fugitives. Even the smallest mistake can provide the clue you need.

Every Movement Comes With a Risk

Fugitives can watch the seeker and move freely around the map. However, moving quickly makes more noise and increases the chance of being discovered.

  • Take a risk and sprint away before the seeker gets too close.

  • Move quietly and deceive the seeker's hearing.

  • Use the environment to hide and break away from pursuit.

  • Lure the seeker into searching in the wrong direction.

An Asymmetric Battle of Wits

The seeker and the fugitives experience the same match with completely different information.

The seeker must predict the location of opponents they cannot clearly see. The fugitives must predict what the seeker has heard and how they will react.

What begins as a simple game of hide-and-seek soon becomes a tense battle of sound, movement, timing, and deception.

Short Rounds Filled With Tension

The seeker must find the fugitives before time runs out. The fugitives must avoid being caught and survive until the end of the round.

Jump into a match without complicated preparation and experience unpredictable situations shaped by the decisions of every player.

Key Features

  • Asymmetric Online PvP — One blindfolded seeker against multiple fugitives

  • Sound-Based Tracking — Use footsteps, echoes, and environmental sounds to locate other players

  • Risk-and-Reward Movement — Moving faster helps you escape, but also makes you easier to detect

  • Psychological Mind Games — Predict what your opponent can see, hear, and understand

  • Simple Rules and Fast-Paced Rounds — Easy to learn, with unpredictable situations in every match

Will you hunt by following the sound, or survive by remaining silent?

store_data.about_the_game:
Veggies Bloody Rampage is a fast-paced action-stealth adventure packed with parkour, dark humor, ridiculous violence, and a story that slowly goes completely off the rails.

Control a tiny tomato with a knife and an unhealthy obsession with revenge. Sneak through kitchens, outsmart pan-wielding chefs, rescue your veggie buddies, and absolutely ruin the day of countless disposable stickmen & other creatures.

Meet Potato, Chili, Radish, Zucchini, and a bunch of other completely normal vegetables. (They're definitely normal.)

Run. Climb. Sneak. Slice. Repeat.

Dig deeper into this weird clay world...

...and try not to question it too much.

"Just remember, little tomato... no one ever calls themselves the villain."

Tiny Warning:

Contains clay-style violence, tomato-fueled rampages, blood, chaotically flying limbs, and an unhealthy amount of stickmen & other creatures being turned into vegetable salads. Also includes weird dreams, unsettling vibes, reality refusing to behave properly, and occasional psychological horror.

(Well, actually, maybe it’s not that scary, idk...)

Tiny Flashy Warning:

Near the end, things get... visually enthusiastic (flashing lights, psychedelic effects, colorful and changing backgrounds). If you have photosensitive epilepsy, be careful.

DEVELOPER NOTE:

Veggies Bloody Rampage is still in development!

Feel free to try the Demo to get a taste of the gameplay, characters, and wonderfully questionable tomato logic. Just keep in mind... the demo only scratches the surface. Most of the madness, horror, and story twists are waiting in the full game.

ALSO THIS GAME Is Made (ok, being made!) with love (and questionable sanity!). Featuring original visuals, original character designs (yes, blobs with oval hands are creative too!), and an original funky electronic soundtrack!

store_data.about_the_game:
TypePuppy is a relaxing, feel-good desktop pet-raising game. A little dog named Puppy lives right on your computer desktop, quietly keeping you company as you go about your daily work and study. There's no complicated controls or competitive pressure — just use your computer as normal (typing, clicking) and you'll grow alongside Puppy without even noticing, collecting your own unique outfits along the way.

Earn Points Through Everyday Interaction

Puppy tracks your keystrokes and mouse clicks in real time and converts them into points. Just keep working or studying as usual, and your points will keep adding up.

Open Chests, Get Outfits

Every time you reach 1,000 points (once every 30 minutes), you can open a mystery chest and receive a random cosmetic item — hats, skins, and more. Items come in four rarity tiers: N, R, SR, and SSR. The higher the tier, the lower the drop rate and the harder it is to obtain.

Drop Rates

N: 90%

R: 9%

SR: 0.9%

SSR: 0.1%

Outfits & Collection

Manage everything you own in "My Items" and switch Puppy's look anytime. Check your collection progress for every item in the "Gallery."

Fusion System

Duplicate lower-tier items are never wasted — combine 10 items of the same rarity in the Synth to obtain one item of the next rarity tier up.

Achievements

The game features a variety of built-in achievements covering total keystrokes, time spent together, items collected, and more. Complete them to record every moment you've spent with Puppy.

Thoughtful Companion Reminders

Puppy says hello the first time you turn on your computer each day, and randomly reminds you to rest and drink water after a while of focused work.You can also customize the timing and content of reminders to make the companionship feel truly your own.

store_data.about_the_game:
The closer you get, the stronger you get. Grazed is an incremental arcade game where to kill you have to get in range of dying. Push your kill combo high enough to ignite absurd powers and chase the highest score. Every run earns upgrades, so you always come back deadlier.

GRAZE & SURVIVE

Bounce through a tight arena, slicing enemies out of the air with twin blades and skimming past danger to keep your combo alive. Every kill climbs it higher, and the higher it climbs, the more the game escalates in your favor.

PUSH YOUR COMBO

Chain enough kills to ignite Hyper Mode: faster, deadlier, glowing red across the whole screen. Push further and Supernova takes over completely.

UPGRADE EVERYTHING

Every run, won or lost, earns shards. Spend them on a sprawling upgrade tree: spinning axe sweeps, a razor-straight iaijutsu slash, chain-reacting static bursts, and lightning strikes that hunt the far side of the arena.

REPEAT, BUT STRONGER

Complete skill-based milestones to unlock Glyphs: permanent buffs like surviving a lethal hit at high combo, or doubling your bounce score for good.

store_data.about_the_game:
This is an interactive visual novel entirely created with AI. Worshiping the Immortal Path and seeking eternal life—this is the dream of every cultivator. Yet Xun Cheng, a cultivation prodigy, mistakenly joins the demonic sect "Tiansha Sect," where, in the eyes of its many elders, he becomes an indispensable "talent." Xun Cheng must find every way to survive—whether by lying low until the very end, restoring the righteous path, or going all the way down the dark road to become the supreme demon lord. Deadly traps, schemes and intrigues, and encounters with heroic maidens—everything depends on your choices.

This is a relaxing casual game that requires no complex operations. Simply watch the cinematics, and when the story branches, make your choice from the options that appear, then watch the outcome of your decision.

If you make a wrong choice and reach a bad ending, just click "Retry" to easily return to the previous choice and try again.

If you want to revisit previous scenes, you can use the "Flowchart" feature to jump back to any earlier decision node, rewatch the scenes, and make a different choice.

Once you've found the correct path, you can enjoy the ending and complete the game. There are five acts in total—just treat this as a lighthearted, interactive movie experience.

store_data.about_the_game:
Team up and push the lane. Lanebound is a fantasy co-op PvE MOBA for 1–3 players—classic mouse controls, no PvP, just you and your friends against the AI.

Features

  • One-lane matches built for co-op: waves, towers, inhibitors, and the core

  • Play solo or with up to 2 friends (3 players total)

  • Steam lobbies, friend invites, and Quick Match

  • Distinct heroes—Warrior, Barbarian, Ranger, Mage, Rogue, Support, and Engineer

  • Gold, items, ability leveling, and coordinated teamfights

  • Server-authoritative online play over Steam

How it plays Right-click to move and attack. Cast with Q/W/E/R. Recall, shop, and coordinate the push. Edge-pan the camera and fight like a classic MOBA—designed for teamwork, not player-vs-player.

Gather your party. Hold the line. Break the core.

store_data.about_the_game:
The endless grind of a Massively Multiplayer Online Roleplaying Game repackaged as an idle game

Chase the high of getting your next upgrade, catering your build to new content, and exploring tons of mechanics and systems to ascend to the endgame in MMO Simulator: ASCENSIONS.

Your character continues to grind even while you're playing another game, or even offline, keeping the gains constant, and the numbers rising.

Endless collectibles and upgrades to outfit your character, and your build

Across MMO Simulators 18 Zones, you'll collect and experience

  • 10 Gear slots to outfit in the best gear you can find

  • 13 Grinding Zones with progressively better loot

  • 9 Playable classes to mix and match

  • Resources to gather and spend

  • Your own Town that passively earns you resources

  • Buy and upgrade your Ships in Port and send them on expeditions for powerful Remnants

  • Over 50 pets - Each with a unique ability

  • 6 Steeds to boost your stats

  • Over 50 random encounters with powerful rewards

  • Over 40 Trinkets

  • Crafting - Allowing you to create powerful Consumable items and keys to enter dungeons and raids

  • 13 Bosses & 10 Boss Minigames

  • 13 Factions to grind Reputation with and earn unique Materials from

  • Over 20,000 unique Title combinations that provide passive stat boosts

  • A simple Questing system to boost your XP and Reputation

  • Countless build options

  • An infinitely scaling ENDGAME zone

  • An ascension system with over 50 unlocks to keep you grinding well after you reach the Endgame

MMO Simulator: ASCENSIONS rewards you for being a part of the process, but your contribution is up to you

Minmaxxing is encouraged, and you'll climb faster by catering your build and decisions to the Zone you're currently grinding, but passive grinding also gets the job done, allowing MMO Simulator to be the perfect second monitor game, or your next obsession.

While you're offline, your character continues Grinding, and your Town and Ships continue earning you rewards for when you return.

Like any good MMO experience, MMO Simulator: ASCENSIONS just keeps going as long as you're willing to grind

Once you've reached Level 100 and earned the best Gear in the land, you still have The Ascent to contend with. An endlessly scaling Zone that just keeps getting harder, earning you Ascension Stars.

When you've finally had enough, visit The Crucible to spend your Ascension Stars and walk one of 4 Paths Of Ascension, granting you permanent boosts and unlocks to carry into your next run. You didn't think you were done, did you?

You're in the best place to start your MMO Simulator: ASCENSIONS journey

Purchasing MMO Simulator on Steam grants you all of these exclusive benefits

  • Equip up to 2 Pets at a time!

  • Exclusive MIMIC Pet - Copies the effect of your other equipped pets!

  • Exclusive playable Class - The Merchant specializes in earning you Gold, and spending it for powerful effect

  • An exclusive Steam only collectible type

  • Bonus Trinket: Supporter's Spork is equipped in its own Trinket Slot so you're never without it!

  • Exclusive Title "The Generous Soul" provides +35% Gold gains, and +35% Mana gains

  •  4  6 Gear Loadouts

  •  5  7 buyable Ships in Port

  • Achievements

  • Cloud saving via Steam

MMO Simulator: ASCENSIONS is a one-time cost with no purchasable boosts or items beyond initial purchase

Be sure that you'll never need to open your wallet to make progress in MMO Simulator. Every Grind, and every new item will be a product of your determination, and not a product of endless cash grabs.
